1452674698.readme_html:
StartupOS

Your startup's private AI workspace - running on your own computer.
Bookings with WhatsApp reminders · inventory alerts · client portal · deadlines · Google reviews · receipt extraction · support-inbox triage · AI cost estimates from machine drawings · meeting summaries - with a 24/7 AI assistant that can do anything the screens can (every change waits for your Confirm) and a glossy iPhone-style UI.

Caution

⚠️ Student-grade project - no one is liable for anything

StartupOS is a student-grade project, built for learning and demonstration. It is provided "as is", without any warranty of any kind, and it has not been audited, certified or tested for production, legal, financial, tax, medical or engineering use.

Neither the developer(s) nor any AI - the Gemma models, Claude, or any other model or service the app uses - is liable for any damage or loss of any kind, including (but not limited to): missed bookings or reminders, missed tax filings or licence renewals and the penalties that follow, wrong cost estimates or prices, wrong extracted invoice data, e-mails or WhatsApp messages sent or not sent, lost customers, lost money, lost data, or reputational harm.

AI output can be wrong or invented. A human must check every result before relying on it. You use StartupOS entirely at your own risk.

Released under the MIT License - free to use, copy and modify, with no warranty and no liability.

Every admin must accept the Terms & Conditions before the app can be used - and if any admin declines, the entire operation halts (pages, public links, background jobs, reminders, AI and outgoing messages) until the Terms are accepted.

Contents
✨ Features 🚀 Quick start 👋 First run
🧠 The AI 🛡️ Spam protection & queueing 🏗️ How it fits together
🧩 Feature guides ⚙️ Configuration 🧰 Everyday commands
💾 Backups & updates 🔐 Security 📜 Terms in short
🩺 Troubleshooting 🛠️ Development 📁 Project structure
📄 License

✨ Features

Feature Made for What it does
🧮 Cost estimator workshops, manufacturers Upload machine drawings (images/PDF). The AI lists the components, asks you whenever it does not understand the drawing, searches the internet for prices and shows the machine cost as a low / likely / high range with sources.
📅 Bookings clinics, salons, tutors Appointments, free-slot finder, WhatsApp confirmations and reminders (no-shows cost money), optional public booking page, no-show statistics.
📦 Inventory shops on a notebook or Excel Stock levels, quick sales/purchases, Excel import with AI column mapping, low-stock alerts, reorder suggestions and supplier orders.
💼 Clients freelancers, agencies Client portal with proposals (accept/decline), invoices, payment status, UPI links, shared files, AI-drafted reminders.
⏰ Deadlines everyone Tax filings, licence renewals, contract and insurance expiry with reminders before each one, AI suggestions, dates extracted from contracts, calendar export.
⭐ Reviews product sellers, local businesses Asks every customer for a Google review after a purchase, alerts you about bad reviews, drafts polite replies with AI.
🧾 Receipts everyone Photos and PDFs of invoices/receipts become clean spreadsheet rows; exports for Excel, CSV, QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho Books and Tally.
📥 Support inbox online shops Fetches customer e-mails, sorts them by urgency and topic, drafts replies - a person approves every answer.
🎥 Meetings everyone Upload a meeting video of any length → transcript, summary, decisions and action items, stored in PostgreSQL + pgvector and searchable.

Around every feature

  • 🤖 AI assistant, 24/7 - a chat panel on every page that knows your business, runs actions (always behind a confirmation card), highlights the exact button or field you are looking for, gives guided tours and proactive tips, and keeps working in the background while you do other things. With no AI engine reachable it still answers from the offline knowledge base.
  • 🏝️ Dynamic Island - the black pill at the top shows live activity: background jobs with progress, new alerts, AI engine changes. Notifications arrive live, without reloading.
  • 🧭 AI onboarding - on the first run the AI asks what your startup does, names the app (asking again until you give a name), double-checks anything unclear, shows a summary before applying anything, and sorts the features for your kind of business (sell products? the Review manager goes to the top).
  • 👥 Multi-admin approvals - renaming the startup or changing its description needs every admin's approval, after an AI risk review: lost brand recognition, reviews and SEO, the "fraud company" look of frequent renames, and your outstanding dues. The AI's warnings come in a box with "I understand, continue" / "I don't want to, go back".
  • 🎨 Light, dark and system themes, frosted-glass iOS look, works on phones and desktops.

🚀 Quick start

You need: a 64-bit computer with 8 GB RAM (16 GB recommended for the local Gemma model), about 15 GB free disk (about 5 GB without the local model) and internet for the first start. The setup script installs Docker for you when it is missing (it asks first).

Open a terminal inside this folder and run one command:

System Command
🍎 macOS ./setup.sh
🐧 Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, ...) ./setup.sh
🪟 Windows 10 / 11 double-click setup.cmd - or in PowerShell: .\setup.cmd

Answer a few questions (Enter = the default). When it finishes, your browser opens http://localhost:8000 and the script prints the admin user names - plus the password if it generated one. Save that password; it is shown only once (it is also stored in .env).

Setup options (both scripts)
setup.sh setup.cmd / setup.ps1 Effect
-y, --yes -Yes No questions: use the defaults (installs Docker if missing, generates the admin password)
--no-local-llm -NoLocalLlm Do not run Gemma in Docker (saves 2-8 GB of memory and disk)
--model TAG -Model TAG Local model, e.g. gemma3:1b (small, text only), gemma3:4b, gemma3:12b
--port N -Port N Serve StartupOS on http://localhost:N instead of 8000
--no-browser -NoBrowser Do not open the browser at the end
--native - Run without Docker (see Development)
--help Get-Help .\setup.ps1 Show the help

The scripts are safe to run again at any time - to update, to repair, or after editing .env.

What the setup script does, step by step
  1. Checks the system (macOS, Linux or WSL; Intel/AMD or ARM) and Docker. If Docker is missing it asks, then installs it - macOS: Docker Desktop via Homebrew or the official Docker.dmg; Linux: Docker Engine + Compose plugin via https://get.docker.com; Windows: Docker Desktop via winget (WSL 2). It starts Docker and waits for it. Docker Compose v2.20+ is required (installed automatically on Linux when missing or too old).
  2. Picks the local AI model from your memory: below 10 GB RAM the small text-only gemma3:1b, otherwise gemma3:4b (--model overrides, --no-local-llm switches it off).
  3. Creates .env from .env.example: startup name (optional - the AI asks on the first run), admin user name, e-mail and password (typed twice, hidden - or generated), more admins, optional Anthropic API key, the LAN Gemma gateway (default http://192.168.0.101:8000/v1 with the gateway key) and bundled Mailpit or your own SMTP server. It generates SECRET_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and SEARXNG_SECRET and makes the file private (chmod 600 / Windows ACL). An existing .env is never overwritten - only new settings are appended.
  4. Checks the ports (8000, Mailpit 8025, Ollama 11434) and picks free ones.
  5. Builds and starts PostgreSQL + pgvector, Mailpit, SearXNG, Ollama and the StartupOS image (with the minified Tailwind CSS and JavaScript built inside the image).
  6. Waits until the app answers (/healthz), prints a summary and opens your browser. The Gemma model keeps downloading in the background (docker compose logs -f ollama-pull).

👋 First run

flowchart LR
    L["Sign in<br/>(admin from .env)"] --> T{"Terms &<br/>Conditions"}
    T -- "I accept" --> O["AI onboarding<br/>asks about your startup<br/>and names the app"]
    T -- "I decline" --> H["⛔ Entire operation halted<br/>until the Terms are accepted"]
    O --> S["Summary box<br/>I understand, continue /<br/>I don't want to, go back"]
    S --> D["Dashboard<br/>features sorted for<br/>your type of business"]
Loading
  1. Open http://localhost:8000 and sign in with an admin from .env (ADMIN_1_USERNAME / ADMIN_1_PASSWORD).
  2. Accept the Terms & Conditions. Every admin listed in .env must accept them. If any admin declines, everything halts - pages, public links, background jobs, reminders, AI processing and outgoing messages - until the Terms are accepted.
  3. Talk to the onboarding AI. What does your startup do, for whom, do you sell products or services? The AI only names the app from a name you actually give - if you don't mention one, it asks again (and suggests names if you have none). It double-checks anything unclear ("Just to be sure ..."), then shows a summary with "I understand, continue" / "I don't want to, go back". Only after you continue is the profile saved (PostgreSQL + pgvector) and the name written to STARTUP_NAME in .env.
  4. Your features, sorted for you. Product sellers get the Review manager first, clinics and salons get Bookings, freelancers get Clients, workshops get the Cost estimator. Change the order or hide features in Settings → Features.
  5. Later name or description changes go through Settings: the AI explains the risks first, and the change applies only after every admin has approved it.

🧠 The AI

Every AI request walks down this chain until one engine answers:

flowchart LR
    R(["Your request"]) --> G{"Spam guard<br/>rate limits · duplicates · size"}
    G -- "ok" --> Q["Priority queue<br/>interactive › normal › background"]
    Q --> A["① Gemma on your LAN<br/>192.168.0.101:8000 (OpenAI-compatible)"]
    A -- "down · busy · no answer" --> B["② Gemma 3 in Docker<br/>(bundled Ollama)"]
    B -- "down · busy" --> C["③ Claude<br/>(optional key, daily budget)"]
    C -- "unavailable" --> K["④ Offline knowledge<br/>pgvector search + rules"]
Loading
# Engine Configure in .env Notes
① Gemma on your LAN PRIMARY_LLM_BASE_URL (default http://192.168.0.101:8000/v1), PRIMARY_LLM_API_KEY (default: the gateway key change-me-gateway-key), PRIMARY_LLM_MODEL=gemma Any OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama). Reads images (receipts, drawings). A dead host fails over in 3 s; a request that hangs gets one automatic retry (a load-balanced gateway routes it to a free backend). off disables it.
② Gemma 3 in Docker LOCAL_LLM_MODEL (chosen from your RAM), COMPOSE_PROFILES=local-llm Runs on CPU in Docker. On a Mac, a natively installed Ollama is much faster: LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1.
③ Claude ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_MODEL (default claude-opus-5-5), ANTHROPIC_DAILY_BUDGET_USD (default 5) Only used when a key is set. Spending is capped per day; Anthropic's server-side refusal fallback is enabled.
④ Offline knowledge - No engine reachable? The assistant answers from the pgvector knowledge base (help, your profile, meetings, estimates) and every feature falls back to rules - the app stays useful offline.

An engine that fails cools down (15 s, doubling to 5 min) and background probes bring it back automatically. A single request that is too long for an engine, or one bad answer, never rests the engine for everyone else - only that request moves on to the next engine. Settings → AI & integrations shows every engine's state, context window, the queue, today's usage and estimated cost.

Context windows. Self-hosted models answer within a fixed window for prompt and answer together - the LAN gateway runs Gemma with 8192 tokens. StartupOS reads the window from the server (llama.cpp and vLLM report it), otherwise assumes 8192, and you can set it yourself with PRIMARY_LLM_CONTEXT / LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT. The assistant sizes every prompt to fit: with a small window it describes the actions that matter most for your question and page (ranked by meaning, not just keywords), finds any other action with its built-in tool finder, and keeps the most recent part of the conversation - so all 212 actions stay reachable. The bundled Ollama runs with 8192 tokens; a native Ollama defaults to 4096 (start it with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192, or set LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT=4096).

Note

The LAN gateway key change-me-gateway-key is the gateway's default - anyone on your Wi-Fi can use it. Set your own key on the gateway and put the same value in PRIMARY_LLM_API_KEY. When Claude or a web-search API is used, the text, images or documents of that request are sent to that provider; leave the keys empty if you do not want that.

🤖 The assistant can do everything the screens can

Anything you can click in StartupOS you can also just ask for - 212 actions across every feature and Settings (only file uploads stay on the page: drawings, receipt photos, recordings, spreadsheets).

Just say… What happens
"Add a client named Rahul seeking software solutions paying 1 lakh" Card: add client Rahul (needs saved as notes)
"Rahul paid 20000 by UPI for the website invoice" Card: record ₹20,000 on Rahul's matching invoice
"Make a proposal for Mohit: annual software support at 80000" Card: the AI writes the lines and saves a draft proposal
"I sold 3 lavender candles" · "We received 10 more" Card: stock goes down / up
"Book Ravi for teeth cleaning tomorrow at 10 am" · "Move Ravi's appointment to the day after tomorrow at 3 pm" Card: booking created / moved
"Add a deadline: PF return on the 15th, monthly" Card: deadline with reminders
"Mark the Shree Packaging bill as paid by bank transfer" Card: bill marked paid
"Estimate the cost of a 2 m belt conveyor with a 0.5 HP motor" Card: estimate started; the AI lists parts and prices them
"Move Inventory to the top of the menu" · "Rename the startup" Card - a rename first shows the AI risk warnings and needs every admin

Built so a small model cannot get it wrong quietly

  • Nothing changes without you: every change is a card with Confirm / Cancel; the card is checked before it is shown, so you never get one that can only fail ("Mohit isn't a client yet - add him first?").
  • No fake "done": if the AI says it created something without actually doing it, it is corrected - or you are told plainly that nothing was changed.
  • Understands how people talk: names instead of numbers ("Rahul's website invoice"), plurals ("lavender candles"), "Tax" vs "tax", "annually", "mark as spam", "top of the menu".
  • Shows instead of tells: "where do I change the startup name?" → a "Show me" button that dims the page and spotlights the right control - even on another page. Ask for a tour of any page.
  • Knows your business: your profile, live numbers from every feature, and a pgvector knowledge base.
  • Works in the background: long tasks run as jobs with live progress in the Dynamic Island.

Every one of these was checked against the real Gemma 3 12B on the LAN gateway: a natural request, the card, Confirm, then the result verified in the app's own data.

🛡️ AI spam protection & queueing

Spam protection runs before every AI request a person triggers:

Protection Setting (default)
Requests per minute per admin AI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE (30)
Requests per minute per IP on public pages (booking, client portal) AI_PUBLIC_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE (5)
Longest text per request AI_MAX_INPUT_CHARS (8000)
Same text from the same person within 10 s refused as a duplicate
3 limit hits within 10 minutes 5-minute pause + one alert to the admins

Content coming in from the public - support e-mails, booking forms, portal messages, reviews - gets a spam score from cheap signals first (links, spam phrases, SHOUTING, repetition, suspicious domains, disposable e-mail addresses, honeypot fields, minimum fill time). Clear spam is dropped; only borderline cases are double-checked by the AI, at background priority.

Queueing: each engine handles AI_CONCURRENCY_PRIMARY (2), AI_CONCURRENCY_LOCAL (1) and AI_CONCURRENCY_ANTHROPIC (4) requests at once; the rest wait in a priority queue (interactive → normal → background, first come first served). Interactive requests wait at most 20 s and normal ones 60 s before spilling to the next engine; background work waits for the free local engines instead of spending Claude money. You see your position live ("Queued #3"), and identical requests already running are answered once for everybody.

🧩 Feature guides

🧮 Cost estimator - AI cost of a machine from its drawings
  1. Upload drawings (images or PDF; several at once) and give the estimate a title.
  2. The AI reads them and lists the components with quantities, materials and sizes. If it does not understand the drawing, it simply asks you - what the machine is, what a part is made of - and your answers go into the next round (also when the vision engines are offline).
  3. It researches prices on the internet for every component (the bundled private SearXNG first, then Brave / SerpAPI / Tavily if you add keys, then DuckDuckGo), converts currencies, removes outliers, and adds labour, overhead, contingency and margin. Running without Docker? There is no SearXNG then, and DuckDuckGo usually refuses automated searches - add a search key (BRAVE_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY or SERPAPI_KEY; Brave and Tavily have free tiers) or set SEARXNG_URL, otherwise parts stay "no price found" and you type prices in yourself.
  4. You get a low / likely / high total, a cost breakdown, the source of every price, and CSV / Excel export. Edit any component or price and the totals update.

Pages are fetched politely (robots.txt, rate limits, private network addresses blocked). Estimates are not quotes - always confirm prices with suppliers.

📅 Bookings - WhatsApp reminders so fewer people no-show
  • Services, staff, customers and appointments; a free-slot finder respects business hours.
  • Reminders go out automatically before each appointment (default 24 h and 2 h) by WhatsApp, with e-mail as a fallback - each one is sent exactly once.
  • No-show tracking with lost-revenue statistics and a risk badge per booking.
  • Optional public booking page and confirm/cancel links for customers (needs PUBLIC_BASE_URL - see Links for your customers below).
  • A completed appointment can trigger a Google review request (Reviews feature).
📦 Inventory - reorder alerts for shops that used a notebook or Excel
  • Import your Excel/CSV: the AI maps your column names (item, qty, MRP, reorder level ...) to the right fields; you preview before anything is saved.
  • Record sales and purchases in a tap; low-stock and out-of-stock alerts (plus a morning digest).
  • Reorder suggestions from your real sales speed and supplier lead time; AI-drafted purchase orders you approve before they are e-mailed to the supplier.
💼 Clients - a portal for freelancers
  • Proposals (AI first draft from a short brief), invoices, payments and files per client.
  • A private client portal link: clients see proposals (accept / decline), invoices and payment status, shared files, and can send you a message. UPI payment links when UPI_ID is set.
  • Overdue invoices are detected every morning; polite reminder e-mails drafted by AI.
⏰ Deadlines - tax, licences, contracts
  • Every deadline with reminders before it is due (default 30, 7 and 1 days), recurring deadlines roll over automatically, calendar (.ics) export.
  • "Suggest deadlines": typical filings for your country and business (labelled "verify with your accountant").
  • Extract from a contract: upload it and the AI finds expiry, renewal and notice dates.
⭐ Reviews - Google reviews after every purchase
  • Set GOOGLE_PLACE_ID. After a purchase or appointment, the customer gets a friendly review request by WhatsApp or e-mail with your Google review link.
  • No review gating: every customer gets the same request - Google's policies forbid filtering out unhappy customers.
  • Bad reviews trigger an immediate alert and an AI-drafted reply you can edit and post. With GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY the latest Google reviews are imported automatically.
🧾 Receipts - photos and PDFs to spreadsheet rows
  • Drop in photos or PDFs; Gemma 3 reads them (vision) and extracts vendor, GSTIN/tax ID, number, dates, line items, taxes and totals - with a confidence score per field.
  • Totals are cross-checked, duplicates detected, and you approve each document.
  • Export to CSV, Excel, QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho Books or Tally (import templates - verify in your accounting software). Works offline with text-layer PDFs and OCR.
📥 Support inbox - triage for online shops
  • Connect a mailbox: IMAP_HOST, IMAP_PORT (993), IMAP_USERNAME, IMAP_PASSWORD, IMAP_FOLDER (INBOX), IMAP_SSL=true - for Gmail imap.gmail.com with an App Password. It is checked every IMAP_POLL_MINUTES (5). No mailbox? Paste e-mails, upload .eml files or load demo e-mails. Settings has a Test IMAP button.
  • Every e-mail is spam-checked first, then sorted by urgency and topic (orders, refunds, shipping, complaints ...), with an SLA timer; urgent ones alert you at once.
  • The AI drafts a reply using your profile and knowledge base - nothing is sent until a person clicks "Approve & send".
🎥 Meetings - any length, summarised and searchable
  • Upload a recording of any length: it is sent in resumable chunks, audio is processed in 10-minute pieces, so memory stays flat even for multi-hour videos.
  • Local speech-to-text with faster-whisper (WHISPER_MODEL: small by default) or any OpenAI-compatible transcription server (WHISPER_REMOTE_URL); or upload a transcript.
  • Summary, key points, decisions and action items (one click turns an action item into a deadline), stored in PostgreSQL + pgvector: search all meetings or "ask this meeting".
  • Ask everyone's consent before recording.
🔗 Links for your customers (PUBLIC_BASE_URL)

Booking confirm pages, the client portal and review click tracking send customers links to this app - those must work outside your computer, so they are only sent when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is set. While it is empty, customers get a direct Google review link or are asked to reply on WhatsApp.

  • Same Wi-Fi only: BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 and PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://<your-LAN-IP>:8000, then docker compose up -d.
  • Anywhere (HTTPS tunnel): cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000, ngrok http 8000 or tailscale funnel 8000 - put the https address into PUBLIC_BASE_URL. A tunnel exposes the sign-in page too: use strong passwords (or argon2 hashes).
📧 E-mail and 💬 WhatsApp

E-mail - alerts are e-mailed to every admin with an ADMIN_<n>_EMAIL.

  • Out of the box (SMTP_HOST empty) mail goes to the bundled Mailpit server: read it at http://localhost:8025 - nothing leaves your computer.
  • Real delivery: set SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_SECURITY (starttls / ssl / none), SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_FROM (e.g. Gmail smtp.gmail.com:587 + an App Password).
  • Settings has a Send test e-mail button.

WhatsApp - WHATSAPP_PROVIDER:

  • console (default): nothing is sent automatically; every message gets a Send via WhatsApp (wa.me) link so you can send it with one click.
  • meta: WhatsApp Cloud API (WHATSAPP_META_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID); messages outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window need an approved template (WHATSAPP_META_TEMPLATE).
  • twilio: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM.

Only message customers who agreed to it, and follow WhatsApp's business policies.

⚙️ Configuration (.env)

.env is the single configuration file - the admin accounts and the startup name live only there. .env.example documents every setting with its default.

Setting Meaning
ADMIN_<n>_USERNAME, ADMIN_<n>_PASSWORD, _EMAIL, _PHONE, _NAME The admin accounts. Add ADMIN_2_... for more admins.
STARTUP_NAME Written by the app after onboarding / an approved rename.
SECRET_KEY Signs sessions and forms (generated). Changing it signs everybody out.
APP_PORT, BIND_ADDRESS Where the app is published (127.0.0.1:8000).
PUBLIC_BASE_URL Customer-reachable address; empty = no customer links to this app.
PRIMARY_LLM_*, LOCAL_LLM_*, ANTHROPIC_* The AI engines (see The AI).
AI_* Spam protection and queueing.
SMTP_*, IMAP_*, WHATSAPP_*, TWILIO_* E-mail and WhatsApp.
COMPOSE_PROFILES local-llm runs Gemma in Docker; empty switches it off.
  • The app re-reads .env within a second: new admins, passwords and API keys work without a restart. Docker-level settings (APP_PORT, BIND_ADDRESS, COMPOSE_PROFILES, POSTGRES_*, APP_UID/APP_GID) need docker compose up -d.
  • Quote values with spaces in single quotes: SMTP_FROM='Acme <a@acme.example>'. Values containing $ (argon2 hashes) must be single-quoted. Put comments on their own line.

💾 Backups, updates and resetting

Back up .env plus the database and files:

docker compose exec db pg_dump -U startupos -d startupos -Fc -f /tmp/startupos.dump
docker compose cp db:/tmp/startupos.dump ./startupos.dump
docker compose cp app:/app/data ./data-backup

Restore the database:

docker compose cp ./startupos.dump db:/tmp/startupos.dump
docker compose exec db pg_restore -U startupos -d startupos --clean --if-exists /tmp/startupos.dump

Update: get the new version of this folder (keep your .env) and run the setup script again - only new settings are added, the image is rebuilt and the containers recreated.

Reset: docker compose down removes the containers but keeps all data; docker compose down -v deletes everything (database, uploads, models) - run the setup script afterwards for a fresh start (your .env and admins stay). Ask every admin to accept the Terms again: docker compose exec app python scripts/manage.py reset-terms --yes.

🔐 Security

  • 🔑 .env holds the keys to everything. The setup makes it readable only by you (chmod 600 / Windows ACL) and .gitignore keeps it out of git. Never share it.
  • 🏠 Local by default: the app and Mailpit are published on 127.0.0.1 only; the database, SearXNG and Ollama stay inside Docker (Ollama's API only on 127.0.0.1).
  • 🔒 Sign-in: signed session cookies, session-fixation protection, login throttling, constant-time password checks, optional argon2 hashes; changing a password in .env ends that admin's sessions.
  • 🧱 Every form and API write needs a CSRF token; a strict Content-Security-Policy (no inline scripts), X-Frame-Options: DENY and other security headers are always on.
  • 🤖 AI abuse protection: rate limits, input caps, duplicate suppression, flood cooldowns; public forms have honeypots, signed timestamps and per-IP limits.
  • 🔗 Customer links use long random tokens and are only sent when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is set.
  • 🐳 Container hardening: unprivileged user, no-new-privileges, minimal capabilities, tini as PID 1.
  • 🌐 Web pages fetched for price research are checked against private network addresses (SSRF protection) and robots.txt.

Problem Fix

POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing in .env Run the setup script once; it adds missing secrets.
The app keeps restarting docker compose logs app shows why - usually .env (no admin with a password, missing SECRET_KEY).
Database password authentication failed .env was recreated while the old database volume exists. Run the setup script - it re-syncs the password.

"AI is busy" Every engine's queue is full: raise AI_MAX_QUEUE / AI_CONCURRENCY_* or add an engine.

🛠️ Native and development mode

Without Docker (macOS / Linux): ./setup.sh --native checks for Python 3.12+, creates .venv, installs the packages, creates .env (asking for DATABASE_URL), builds the CSS/JS, runs scripts/manage.py check and starts the app. You need PostgreSQL 15+ with pgvector:

brew install postgresql@17 pgvector && brew services start postgresql@17      # macOS
docker run -d --name startupos-db -e POSTGRES_USER=startupos -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me \
  -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 pgvector/pgvector:pg17                                # any OS, database only

DATABASE_URL looks like postgresql+asyncpg://startupos:change-me@127.0.0.1:5432/startupos.

Development:

python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_assets.py --watch     # Tailwind CSS + esbuild, rebuilds on change
.venv/bin/python -m app --reload                     # restarts on code changes
.venv/bin/python scripts/manage.py check             # configuration, database, AI engines

Tests - 943 of them, about a minute (need PostgreSQL + pgvector; they create their own database and never touch the network, an AI engine, SMTP or WhatsApp):

TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://startupos@127.0.0.1:5432/startupos_test .venv/bin/pytest -q

1452312837.readme_html:
Agentic World Simulator

Test a startup's strategy inside a simulated world before trying it in the real one.

Hundreds of thousands of agents (consumers, companies and stock-market traders) pursue goals, learn and influence each other in a market calibrated to live news, markets and natural hazards, on an interactive 3D globe. An AI layer reads the world every day and explains what it means for your startup.

Features · Screenshots · Quick start · AI hierarchy · Simulation · License · Disclaimer

Caution

This is a student-grade project, provided "as is", with no warranty and no liability. It was built as a learning exercise. It is not a commercial product, not production-ready, not audited and not maintained. Nothing it shows (forecasts, probabilities, simulations, AI-generated text, hazard alerts or insurance hints) is financial, investment, legal, insurance, medical or safety advice, and it must not be used for real-world decisions. The author(s) accept no responsibility or liability whatsoever for any loss or damage arising from its use. Released under the MIT License. Read the full disclaimer before using it.

Features
3D globe, light & dark Countries coloured by today's market move, the 1-month move, AI-scored news sentiment, news volume or simulated consumer confidence. Earthquakes, cyclones, floods, wildfires and volcanoes appear as alert-coloured points with pulsing rings. Your HQ is marked, and arcs show where your startup could help.
First-run onboarding The AI interviews you about the startup: what it sells, whether it can ship and where, its HQ and target markets. Every recommendation is then filtered to what the startup can actually do; a startup with no physical products is never told to ship products and gets market insights instead.
Reliable news, once a day 16 feeds from established outlets (CNN, The Times of India, The New York Times, BBC, The Guardian, Al Jazeera, Economic Times and others) are collected once every 24 hours, and fetched before anything else on the very first run.
AI insights with timestamps Daily global brief, market outlooks ("the Indian market is down, what happens next?"), region reports, disaster impact analyses, HQ risk alerts with insurance suggestions, "how people are reacting" persona reports and simulation reports. Every one is stored in PostgreSQL with its date and time.
Grounded forecasts Market outlooks combine a Monte Carlo forecast on the real index, an agent-based forecast from the calibrated world model, headlines retrieved with pgvector and persona reactions. The AI writes bear/base/bull scenarios that must stay consistent with those numbers.
Disaster impact For a significant event the app estimates the local market and currency reaction, what people need, supply-chain risks, and whether your startup can help. A simulation compares helping genuinely, helping promotionally (backlash risk) and not helping.
HQ location risk Checks seismic activity near your HQ against its normal rate (a statistical test), the 50-year earthquake history and 7-day weather extremes, then warns you and suggests insurance cover.
Agent-based simulation lab Run scenarios such as a market crash, an earthquake plus a relief campaign, a price war or a launch push, with up to 5 million consumer agents across worker processes. Crashes, bubbles, herding and panic cascades emerge from agent interactions and are detected automatically.
Calibrated to reality Agent counts and incomes come from World Bank data, starting confidence from news sentiment and persona moods, and each stock-market model is fitted to its real index (volatility, fat tails, volatility clustering).
Live & resilient A durable PostgreSQL task queue, a scheduler, live notifications over Server-Sent Events, an AI failover hierarchy and layered spam protection in front of the AI.

Quick start

1. Configure

copy .env.example .env

Fill in .env:

Variable What to put
OPENAI_GEMMA_URL the LAN gateway's base_url, e.g. http://192.168.0.101:8000/v1 (several comma-separated URLs allowed)
OPENAI_GEMMA_API_KEY the gateway's api_key
OPENAI_GEMMA_MODEL the gateway's model name, e.g. gemma
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY optional, enables the Anthropic tier

Then change the admin login in config.py (ADMIN_USERS; the default is admin / admin123).

2a. Run everything in Docker

docker compose up -d --build

The first start downloads Gemma 3 4B and EmbeddingGemma (about 4 GB) for the Local Gemma tier.

2b. Or run the app natively on Windows

PostgreSQL and Local Gemma stay in Docker; the app itself runs in a Python 3.13 virtual environment.

py install 3.13
py -V:3.13 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\start-native.ps1

start-native.ps1 starts the database and Local Gemma containers, stops the Docker copy of the app (only one can use port 8000) and runs run.py in a console window. Close the window to stop it.

Note

Use Python 3.13, not 3.15, on Windows. Smart App Control blocks the brand-new 3.15 builds of asyncpg and the Anthropic SDK's JSON parser, because Windows has no reputation for them yet. The 3.13 builds load fine.

3. Open it

Go to http://localhost:8000 and sign in. On the first run the app collects global headlines, then asks about your startup.

The AI hierarchy

Every AI request walks this chain, in this order:

  request
     │
     ▼
  1. OpenAI Gemma  ── Gemma 3 12B behind the LAN gateway, called with the `openai` SDK
     │  unreachable / failing
     ▼
  2. Local Gemma   ── Gemma 3 4B in Ollama on this PC (same OpenAI-compatible API)
     │  unreachable / failing
     ▼
  3. Anthropic     ── Claude (claude-opus-5-5) via the `anthropic` SDK, structured JSON output
     │  unreachable / not configured
     ▼
  4. unavailable   ── "AI is not present": the app refuses to start
  • At startup every tier is probed. If none answers, the app does not run and prints each tier's reason.
  • While running, if every tier drops out the UI locks behind an "AI is not present" screen, background work pauses, and everything resumes automatically when a tier comes back.
  • Slow is not absent. A busy model that times out falls through to the next tier for that request; only an unreachable or misconfigured chain locks the app.
  • A wrong API key keeps that tier's circuit open for 30 minutes, so the gateway isn't hammered with a bad key.
  • If a backend's context window is too small, the request is retried once on the same tier with a condensed prompt.

Spam protection (AI overload guard)

Layer Default
Concurrent AI calls 2; one slot is always kept free for the person using the app
Waiting room 24 queued calls; more are rejected
App-wide AI rate 40 calls per minute (token bucket)
Per-admin AI actions 6 per minute, burst of 3
Identical prompts merged into one call and cached for 15 minutes
Same analysis (e.g. India outlook) reused if less than 15 minutes old
Automatic "market is down" analyses at most 3 per market refresh, most relevant first
Background tasks de-duplicated: the same job is never queued twice; at most 2 simulations queued
Failing tiers circuit breaker: 3 failures → skipped for 2 minutes
Anthropic (paid) daily call and token budget
Inputs prompts capped at 24k characters, chat messages at 2k
API and login 600 requests per minute per IP; 5 failed logins → 15-minute lockout; CSRF header check

How the simulation works

Nothing below is scripted: crashes, trends and herd behaviour emerge from agents interacting.

  • Consumers are vectorised numpy agents on a small-world social network, sharded across worker processes and synchronised every simulated day (bulk-synchronous parallel). Each has an income, price sensitivity, social susceptibility, a personal contagion threshold, equity exposure, confidence, brand awareness and a memory of past experiences with each company.
  • Herding: panic and euphoria spread through social ties by threshold contagion and recover over time. Purchases follow a choice model weighing quality, price against income, awareness, remembered experiences, what friends use, and reputation.
  • Companies set prices and marketing, serve demand within capacity, run campaigns and build reputation; adaptive competitors learn pricing and marketing from profit (a multi-armed bandit).
  • Stock markets: fundamentalist and chartist traders, with opinion herding, trend chasing and strategy switching. They are coupled both ways to consumer confidence, so a market crash can spill into spending and panicking consumers can drag a market down.
  • Calibration: each market model is fitted to its real index by the method of simulated moments. Defaults already reproduce realistic statistics: about 1% daily volatility, fat tails and volatility clustering.
  • Detected patterns: crashes, bubbles (with a right-tailed unit-root test), trader herding, consumer panic cascades, sentiment regime shifts, volatility clustering, fat tails, adoption tipping points, winner-take-all concentration and price wars.

Measured on the author's 16-core laptop: 200,001 consumers plus 160,000 traders on 8 worker processes simulated 120 days in about 5.5 seconds.

│  globe.gl 3D globe · Chart.js · light/dark · live updates (SSE)  │

┌──────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────┐

│  ├─ AI router ─ OpenAI Gemma → Local Gemma → Anthropic → unavail.│
│  │   └─ guard: concurrency · queue · rate · cache · budget       │
│  ├─ intel: onboarding · brief · outlook · geo impact · risk ·    │

│  ├─ data: news · markets · hazards · World Bank · geography      │

└───────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
        │ SQLAlchemy 2 async + asyncpg             │ worker processes
┌───────▼──────────────────────────┐  ┌────────────▼───────────────┐
│ PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector         │  │ Simulation engine (numpy)  │
│ insights · news · markets ·      │  │ consumer shards · traders  │

└──────────────────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────────┘

Data sources

Source Used for Refresh
CNN (text-only edition), The Times of India (3 feeds), The New York Times (2), BBC News (2), The Guardian, Al Jazeera, The Economic Times, The Hindu, CNBC, Deutsche Welle, NPR, The Japan Times headlines for briefs, outlooks and persona agents every 24 hours
Yahoo Finance chart API 30 indices, volatility gauges, currencies, commodities, Bitcoin hourly
USGS Earthquake Hazards Program earthquakes and seismic baselines 15 min / 6 h
GDACS (UN / European Commission) cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts, wildfires 15 min

Configuration

Settings live in config.py; most can be overridden by environment variables or .env.

Setting Default Meaning
ADMIN_USERS {"admin": "admin123"} the only logins (there are no sign-ups); change it
OPENAI_GEMMA_URL / _API_KEY / _MODEL http://192.168.0.101:8000/v1 · empty · gemma AI tier 1 (LAN gateway)
LOCAL_GEMMA_URL / _MODEL http://localhost:11434/v1 · gemma3:4b AI tier 2 (Ollama on this PC)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_MODEL empty · claude-opus-5-5 AI tier 3
AI_STARTUP_POLICY exit exit refuses to start without AI; lock starts with the UI locked
DATABASE_URL postgresql+asyncpg://worldsim:worldsim@localhost:5434/worldsim PostgreSQL (host port 5434)
EMBEDDING_MODEL embeddinggemma embeddings for pgvector search (local fallback if unavailable)
SIM_SHARDS 0 (auto) simulation worker processes
APP_SECRET_KEY built-in dev value session signing; set your own

Refresh intervals, spam-protection limits and simulation limits are plain constants in config.py.

Project structure

agentic world simulation/
├── app/
│   ├── ai/        AI hierarchy router, spam-protection guard, Gemma + Anthropic providers, embeddings, prompts
│   ├── api/       FastAPI routers (auth, system, world, insights, onboarding, simulation, live stream)
│   ├── data/      news, markets, hazards, World Bank, geography
│   ├── intel/     AI pipelines: onboarding, brief, outlook, geo impact, risk, personas, reports
│   ├── sim/       simulation engine: consumers, companies, traders, engine, patterns, calibration
│   ├── tasks/     PostgreSQL task queue, scheduler, job handlers
│   └── main.py    app setup, middleware, startup AI gate
├── static/        single-page app (HTML, CSS, JS) + vendored globe.gl, Chart.js, textures, country shapes
├── docs/          README screenshots
├── config.py      all settings (admin logins, AI hierarchy, limits)
├── run.py         native entry point (checks the AI hierarchy first)
├── start-native.ps1
├── docker-compose.yml · docker-compose.gpu.yml · Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── .env.example

Adding a new prediction type

  1. Describe the JSON you want back in app/ai/prompts.py.
  2. Write the pipeline in app/intel/: gather data, call runtime.ai.generate_json(...), store with save_insight(...).
  3. Register a job in app/tasks/jobs.py, and a schedule in app/tasks/scheduler.py if it should run periodically.
  4. Optionally expose it through /api/insights/analyze and render it in static/js/render.js.

Troubleshooting

The app prints "AI IS NOT PRESENT" and exits

No tier answered. The banner lists each tier's reason. Check the gateway address and key in .env, start Local Gemma with docker compose up -d ollama ollama-pull, or set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

The gateway worked yesterday but not today

Its PC may have received a new address from the router. Copy the new base_url from the gateway window into OPENAI_GEMMA_URL (you can list several, comma-separated), or give that PC a DHCP reservation in the router. Local Gemma keeps answering meanwhile.

"An Application Control policy has blocked this file" on Windows

Smart App Control is blocking a freshly published compiled package. Use the Python 3.13 virtual environment described in the quick start, or run everything in Docker.

Port 8000 is already in use

Only one copy of the app can run at a time. Use either Docker (docker compose up -d) or native (start-native.ps1, which stops the Docker copy for you).

AI analyses are slow

Local Gemma on a CPU takes minutes per analysis; the GPU-backed gateway takes seconds. For Local Gemma on an NVIDIA GPU: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d.

API documentation is available at http://localhost:8000/api/docs after signing in.

ai.title: AuraMind: AI Companion for Wellbeing
ai.reason: The project's primary focus is providing an AI companion to address mental health challenges like intrusive thoughts, OCD, and anxiety, directly benefiting individuals.
ai.summary: AuraMind is a student project designed as an AI companion to help users manage intrusive thoughts, OCD, anxiety, and low mood. It dissects thoughts, separates facts from feelings, and offers an ERP urge-delay coach. The application includes a thought journal, live face and voice interaction, and a learning platform with interactive modules.
ai.problem: It addresses the need for accessible and personalized support for individuals struggling with intrusive thoughts, anxiety, and related mental health challenges.
key_points: Thought dissection separates facts from feelings.
Thought journal stores encrypted thoughts and brain activity.
ERP urge-delay coach helps manage compulsive urges.
Live face and voice interaction provides a more engaging experience.
International support with crisis lines and language options.
Learning platform offers modules and interactive brain map.
ai.audience: Individuals experiencing anxiety, OCD, intrusive thoughts, or low mood

1449718210.readme_html:
AuraMind

A gentle AI companion for intrusive thoughts, OCD, anxiety, low mood, trauma and neurodivergent minds

Meet Aura — she listens, separates facts from fears, tells a real fact-check from a compulsion,
and slowly learns what helps you.


Features · Screenshots · Quick start · How Aura stays safe · Security · Testing & results · Report · Licence


Warning

AuraMind is a student-grade project — not medical care, not therapy, not an emergency service. It comes with no warranty, and no one (the author, contributors or anyone else) is liable for any damages caused by it. It is not free for use: proprietary, all rights reserved. Aura is an AI and can be wrong. Never start, stop or change any medicine based on it — always confirm with a qualified medical practitioner. If you might be in danger, call your local emergency number or a crisis line (built into the app for 44 countries, plus findahelpline.com). See Terms and LICENSE.

🌟 At a glance
🧪 154 automated tests unit, integration, N+1 guards, a 33-test attack suite, 29 failsafe / AI-safety tests and 14 account-isolation tests
🛡️ Security stress test 11 issues found and fixed, 20 attack classes verified — report
🔒 Account isolation audit 7 issues fixed: nothing about one person can reach another account, and sign-in always shows the account as it is now — report
🧠 AI red-team (real model) 49 hard, twisted scenarios — 48/49 in the final run (from 42/49); every safety-critical case is now caught by the deterministic net, not left to the model's mood — report
⚡ 10-minute load test 400 users · 90,246 requests · 0 failures · 150 req/s · p95 78 ms — report
🌍 International 25+ languages, crisis lines for 44 countries, emergency numbers for 110+, country-aware weekends and festivals

✨ Features

For the person
🧠 Thought dissection Splits a thought into facts vs feelings & assumptions, names thinking traps, and gives a verdict: genuine fact-check or compulsion — backed by pgvector, which notices when you've asked "the same worry" before.
📓 Thought journal Every thought you dissect or share with Aura in chat is kept (encrypted) with the brain areas that were active. Reopen any of them later — even via a link — and the list loads more as you scroll.
⏳ ERP urge-delay coach For OCD-style urges Aura suggests delaying the compulsion; the delay is sized to your severity (5 → 10 → 15 min) and grows as you succeed.
🗣️ Live face & voice An animated face (emotions, blinking, gaze, breathing) with lip-sync, a soft female voice (Kokoro or the browser's best voice in the language she's replying in) and hands-free live voice that recovers from microphone hiccups.
🌍 Speaks your language Replies in your language — but one stray word ("no idea", a name) never switches it. Hinglish gets Hinglish, in Latin script.
🕰️ Knows your day Local time and date, weekday or weekend (Fri–Sat and Sat-only weekends included), late nights, the Sunday-evening dip, how long since you last talked, and festivals for hundreds of countries ("Diwali is tomorrow — any plans?").
🎨 Light · Dark · Auto Pick Light or Dark (11 palettes each, all contrast-checked) — or Auto: signed in, Aura chooses calming colours from your mood; signed out, it follows your device.
📚 Learning platform 16 modules / 34 lessons / 25 quiz questions, an interactive brain map, and "Explain it my way" tutoring for dyslexic, autistic and ADHD learners.
🔒 Private insights Cognitive profile, suspected patterns with probabilities and mood trends — visible only to you, never to admins.
📸 Moments & notes Photos/screenshots are virus-scanned, re-encoded, read by Tesseract + Gemma vision; clinical notes keep only mental-health conditions — medications are discarded and the file is never stored.

Safety and care
🚦 Crisis-aware Catches crisis language however it's typed — slang, algospeak, leetspeak, look-alike letters, hidden characters, Hinglish and 20+ languages — and treats a possible overdose as a medical emergency even if they "feel fine".
🪞 No snap judgements Patterns only become "likely" after evidence across several sessions; healthy people are recognised as doing well; OCD harm thoughts are never treated as danger.
💊 Medicine guard General over-the-counter information at most — no doses, amounts or schedules ever reach the screen, even spelled out or split across sentences; nothing about medicines when someone is at risk.
🫂 Trusted contacts Optional caregivers can get a gentle "please check in" message on serious risk — only with consent, never with chat content.
🛟 AI failsafe Everyone sees Aura's live status (Online · Busy · Backup AI · Offline). If a reply is interrupted, cut short, stalls or comes from a backup, you're told — with Try again. Providers fail over automatically.
🧱 Spam protection One AI reply at a time per person, an honest "busy" reply under overload (crises always get through), per-person limits, duplicate/burst detection and a sign-up honeypot.
⚖️ Offender vs. disability Repetition, bursts and typos are first explained by the person's profile (OCD loops, autism, ADHD, dyslexia, distress) and met with support. Only explicit trolling, spam or attacks lead to an escalating, appealable ban — never for someone at risk.

For the team
🛰️ Admin console Live traffic (SSE), AI-provider health with a loud banner when your gateway is down, pseudonymised prevalence/comorbidity charts, AI insights, alerts, bans, audits, system health.
🎚️ Per-person limits Rate limits and queue priority live in PostgreSQL, tuned by the AI per person (severe cases jump the queue); every change is audited and admin overrides win for 7 days.

📸 Screenshots
Light — following a light device Dark
Thought Lab — facts vs feelings, verdict, brain map Thought journal — reopen any thought, with its brain areas
Admin console — pseudonymised, live Appearance — Light · Dark · Auto

💬 How a conversation works

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant P as Person
    participant A as AuraMind
    participant S as Safety net (offline-capable)
    participant L as AI (gateway → Claude → local Gemma)
    P->>A: message
    A->>A: one reply at a time per person
    A->>S: crisis check — every spelling, many languages
    S-->>P: crisis card instantly (overdose = medical emergency)
    A->>L: reply in their language, aware of their day
    L-->>A: streamed words
    A->>S: medicine guard on every clause
    A-->>P: reply streams in (or a clear notice: offline · interrupted · busy · cut short)
    A->>L: silent analysis (facts, feelings, brain regions, risk)
    A-->>P: thought lens, brain map, mood colours
    A->>A: profile · care plan · journal · alerts (with consent)
Loading

🏗️ Architecture

flowchart LR
    B[Browser<br/>Tailwind · Line Awesome · Chart.js<br/>WebAuthn · Web Speech] -->|HTTPS · CSP nonce · CSRF| E
    subgraph App[FastAPI · async]
      E[Edge middleware<br/>bans · flood guard · CSP · no-store] --> S[Session middleware<br/>Redis · one login per account]
      S --> R[Routers<br/>auto-loaded via importlib]
      R --> AI[AI layer<br/>safety · analyser · companion<br/>profile · care · abuse · tutor · failsafe]
      R --> U[Uploads<br/>ClamAV · worker threads · OCR]
    end
    AI -->|priority queue · stall timeouts| G[(AI gateway<br/>Gemma 3 · OpenAI API)]
    AI -.fallback.-> C[(Anthropic Claude)]
    AI -.fallback.-> L[(Local Gemma 3<br/>llama.cpp)]
    R --> P[(PostgreSQL 17<br/>+ pgvector)]
    S --> D[(Redis 7)]
    U --> V[(ClamAV)]
    U --> T[Tesseract OCR]
Loading

AI providers, in order: your OpenAI-compatible gateway (LLM_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) → Anthropic Claude (only if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set) → local Gemma 3 via llama.cpp. A circuit breaker cools down failing providers, a probe re-checks every 20 s, the admin console says exactly which provider is serving and why, and people see a plain Online / Busy / Backup AI / Offline status.

🛟 How Aura stays safe

Layer What it does
1. Deterministic safety net Works with every AI offline. Checks each message as written and normalised (look-alike letters, invisible characters, leetspeak, spaced letters, stretched words); clause-aware negation ("I'm not okay, I want to die" is not negated); dropped pronouns; a friend at risk vs. the user at risk; topics vs. crises; overdoses. Word lists live encrypted in app/data/lexicon.bin.
2. Silent analysis Schema-constrained JSON from the model: risk, thought type, facts vs. interpretations, checking vs. fact-check, brain regions. It can only raise the safety net's risk — except for recognised OCD intrusions, which are capped at "distress".
3. Prompt rules Explicit language, time-of-day awareness, no diagnosis, no clinician claims, no reassurance loops, professional referral for dissociation/psychosis, medical-emergency instructions.
4. Medicine guard Filters every streamed clause before it reaches the screen.
5. Failsafe Fail-over, stall timeouts, honest notices, crisis replies that work offline.
6. Care Crisis lines for 44 countries, pseudonymised admin alerts, consented caregiver alerts.

🔐 Security

  • CSP with per-request nonces + strict-dynamic; no inline styles or handlers; object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none', COOP/CORP, Permissions-Policy, HSTS (with HTTPS); Cache-Control: no-store on all personal data.
  • CSRF: signed double-submit tokens bound to the login token, plus Origin/Referer checks — verified on every write route by the attack suite.
  • Sessions in Redis (opaque HttpOnly cookie, idle + absolute expiry, rotated at login). One login per account — an older device is signed out with "your account was signed in on another device".
  • Only ids are remembered. Sessions and the "choose an account" cookie hold account ids only; the name, profile photo, passkey and status are read from the database on every request, so a rename or new photo shows at once and a deleted account signs out every device with "that account no longer exists". Nothing from one sign-in (AI consent, cached photos) carries over to the next person on a shared browser.
  • Unique usernames, case-insensitive (enforced by the database), with a live availability check while signing up and reserved names (admin, support, therapist, …) blocked.
  • Passwords: HMAC-pepper → bcrypt, timing-equalised. 5 failures ban the IP (login, admin login, change password, delete account); scanner probing is banned automatically.
  • Passkeys (WebAuthn): Windows Hello, Touch ID/Face ID, Android — one per account, user verification required.
  • Encryption at rest: names, e-mails, phones, birthdays, conversations, thoughts, moments, clinical extracts and profiles are Fernet-encrypted; e-mails are looked up through a keyed blind index.
  • Uploads: size limit → magic-byte type check → ClamAV (fail-closed) → full re-encode on worker threads (kills polyglots, strips EXIF/GPS) → served only to the owner, never cached.
  • Rate limiting: per-person limits from PostgreSQL, per-endpoint limits, an async per-IP flood guard, and polite 429s in Aura's voice.
  • Admin sees pseudonyms only (P-XXXXXXXX), aggregate charts, and alerts without chat content.

🚀 Quick start (Windows)

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\services.ps1 -Start

services.ps1 is safe to re-run. It installs anything missing with winget (Python 3.12+, Docker Desktop, Tesseract OCR), starts Docker, creates .env with strong random secrets, picks a free PostgreSQL port, creates .venv, starts PostgreSQL + pgvector, Redis and ClamAV, creates the databases/schema/pgvector prototypes, builds the Tailwind CSS and runs health checks.

Command What it does
.\services.ps1 install + services + database
.\services.ps1 -Start …and launch the app
.\services.ps1 -Status containers + health checks
.\services.ps1 -Stop stop containers (data kept)
.\services.ps1 -Voice also run the Kokoro neural voice container
.\services.ps1 -BuildCss rebuild CSS with the local Tailwind CLI
.venv\Scripts\python run.py start the app (add --reload while editing code)

Then open http://localhost:10000 (change PORT in .env). Admin console: /admin with ADMIN_USERNAME / ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env. Database upgrades run automatically at start-up.

Manual setup (any OS) 
docker compose up -d db redis clamav          # PostgreSQL+pgvector, Redis, ClamAV
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cp .env.example .env                          # fill in secrets (LEXICON_KEY must match app/data/lexicon.bin)
.venv/bin/python -m app.cli init-db --with-test-db
.venv/bin/python run.py

Full stack in containers (Python 3.12 image with Tesseract, fastembed and RapidOCR): docker compose --profile app up -d --build.

🩹 Troubleshooting

  • "Port 10000 is already in use" – run.py names the process holding it. If it's an older AuraMind it offers to stop it and start fresh; otherwise close that terminal, or change PORT in .env.
  • Changes don't show up – restart the app (Ctrl+C, run again). A running copy keeps the code and templates it started with; use python run.py --reload while editing.
  • "Aura · Offline" in the nav – the AI gateway can't be reached. Aura answers with safe pre-written replies and crisis lines still work; the admin console shows why.
  • Live voice stops or doesn't hear you – it needs Chrome or Edge, microphone permission, and an internet connection (the browser's speech service). Aura tells you which one is missing. For the neural Kokoro voice run .\services.ps1 -Voice.
  • WinError 10022 once at start-up with WORKERS above 1 – a harmless Windows quirk while uvicorn restarts a worker. The default WORKERS=1 never shows it.
  • Port 5432 busy – services.ps1 moves PostgreSQL to the next free port and updates .env automatically.
  • "Cannot decrypt lexicon.bin" – LEXICON_KEY in .env must be the key the file was encrypted with.
  • Passkeys / microphone don't work on another device – browsers only allow them on HTTPS or http://localhost. Put AuraMind behind HTTPS (e.g. Caddy) and set WEBAUTHN_RP_ID, WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, ALLOWED_HOSTS, COOKIE_SECURE=true.

ai.title: Local AI Server with Load Balancing
ai.reason: This project provides a tool for managing and distributing AI model workloads across multiple computers, primarily benefiting developers and businesses.
ai.summary: This project creates a local AI server that distributes requests across multiple PCs on a network. It uses a gateway to provide a single access point, automatically switching between PCs based on load and availability. The server uses llama.cpp and supports models like Gemma.
ai.problem: It solves the problem of efficiently running large AI models locally by distributing the workload across multiple machines.
key_points: Automatic load balancing between PCs.
Single access point via a gateway.
Supports multiple AI models (e.g., Gemma).
GPU detection and firewall configuration.
Status monitoring of PC availability and load.
Client-side integration with OpenAI Python library.

1447571590.readme_html:
Local AI server: one link for your whole Wi-Fi / LAN

Each PC runs its own copy of the model. A small Python gateway on this PC gives you one link. Requests go to this PC first and switch to your other PC when this one is busy, overloaded or offline.

phone / laptop / your Python apps
            │
            ▼
   http://<this PC's IP>:8000/v1      ← the single link (gateway.py)
            │
   ┌────────┴─────────┐
   ▼                  ▼
this PC :8080      other PC :8080      (llama-server, same model on both)
first choice       used when this PC is busy or down

Setup on THIS PC

  1. Right-click 1_setup_this_pc.bat and choose Run as administrator. It detects your GPU, downloads llama.cpp into C:\llama, opens the firewall for your home network and prints this PC's IP address.
  2. Open 2_start_server.bat and gateway.py and change the change-me-... keys. In gateway.py, set OTHER_PC_IP.
  3. Double-click 2_start_server.bat. The first run downloads Gemma 3 12B (~8 GB). Wait for server is listening.
  4. Double-click 3_start_gateway.bat. This needs Python installed.

Setup on the OTHER PC

Copy 1_setup_this_pc.bat, setup.ps1 and 2_start_server.bat to it. Then do steps 1 and 3 above. Use the same keys and model as this PC. It doesn't need the gateway.

Using it

  • Python: see client.py. Use pip install openai, then point base_url at http://<this PC's IP>:8000/v1 with your gateway key.
  • Check what's happening: open http://<this PC's IP>:8000/status in any browser. It shows which PCs are online and how many slots are busy.
  • Every reply carries an x-served-by header (this-pc or other-pc).

When does it switch?

This PC is… Request goes to
online, has a free slot, CPU below 90% this PC
all slots busy (default 2 at once) other PC
CPU at or above LOCAL_CPU_LIMIT (90%) other PC
server stopped, crashed or still loading other PC (checked every 5 s, and instantly on errors)
both PCs busy queued on the least busy PC

Tips

  • Other devices can't connect? In Windows Settings → Network, set your Wi-Fi or Ethernet to Private. The firewall rules only apply to private networks.
  • Fixed IPs: reserve both PCs' IPs in your router so the links never change.
  • Bigger model: put unsloth/gemma-3-27b-it-GGUF:Q4_K_M in 2_start_server.bat. It's ~17 GB, so part of it runs from RAM and it'll be slower, especially on the RTX 3060.
  • Update llama.cpp: run 1_setup_this_pc.bat again.
  • The gateway runs on this PC. If this PC is switched off, the link is down. You can still reach the other PC directly at http://<other PC's IP>:8080/v1 with the server key.
  • Don't port-forward these ports to the internet. Use Tailscale for access away from home.

4. Double-click **`3_start_gateway.bat`**. This needs Python installed.

## Setup on the OTHER PC

Copy `1_setup_this_pc.bat`, `setup.ps1` and `2_start_server.bat` to it.
Then do steps 1 and 3 above. Use the **same keys and model** as this PC.
It doesn't need the gateway.

## Using it

- **Python:** see `client.py`. Use `pip install openai`, then point `base_url` at
  `http://<this PC's IP>:8000/v1` with your gateway key.
- **Check what's happening:** open `http://<this PC's IP>:8000/status` in any browser.
  It shows which PCs are online and how many slots are busy.
- Every reply carries an `x-served-by` header (`this-pc` or `other-pc`).

## When does it switch?

| This PC is…                                        | Request goes to                                    |
|----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| online, has a free slot, CPU below 90%             | this PC                                            |
| all slots busy (default 2 at once)                 | other PC                                           |
| CPU at or above `LOCAL_CPU_LIMIT` (90%)            | other PC                                           |
| server stopped, crashed or still loading           | other PC (checked every 5 s, and instantly on errors) |
| both PCs busy                                      | queued on the least busy PC                        |

## Tips

- **Other devices can't connect?** In Windows Settings → Network, set your Wi-Fi or
  Ethernet to **Private**. The firewall rules only apply to private networks.
- **Fixed IPs:** reserve both PCs' IPs in your router so the links never change.
- **Bigger model:** put `unsloth/gemma-3-27b-it-GGUF:Q4_K_M` in `2_start_server.bat`.
  It's ~17 GB, so part of it runs from RAM and it'll be slower, especially on the RTX 3060.
- **Update llama.cpp:** run `1_setup_this_pc.bat` again.
- **The gateway runs on this PC.** If this PC is switched off, the link is down.
  You can still reach the other PC directly at `http://<other PC's IP>:8080/v1`
  with the server key.
- Don't port-forward these ports to the internet. Use Tailscale for access away from home.

1448195629.readme_html:
ClassNest

The AI-powered classroom for small schools & tuition centres

Live classes · AI notes · AI tests · AI tutor · holiday-aware scheduling · auto-attendance · fees & payroll · PTMs
with a private AI that runs on your own GPU in Docker — or Claude when you'd rather not run it locally.


Quick start · Screenshots · Classes & subjects · Demo school · AI models · Features · Security · Tested · Load test

Warning

Student-grade project. Use at your own risk. ClassNest is a learning / demonstration project built by a student. It is provided “as is”, without any warranty of any kind, and it has not been professionally audited.

No one is liable for any damages caused by this app: not the author, not the developers, not the contributors, not anyone. That includes data loss, data breaches, financial loss, wrong grades or attendance, AI mistakes or any other harm, however it is caused.

Have it reviewed by professionals before using it with real children's data or money. The code is released under the MIT License; the full disclaimer is in DISCLAIMER.md and on the app's built-in Terms & Conditions page (/p/terms), which cannot be deleted from the admin panel. For licensing questions, or a separate licence with different terms, contact the author: DHURJATI-JS.

🌟 At a glance

🎓 Teach

  • Google-Meet-style live classes inside the app, recorded
  • AI class notes from captions + chat
  • AI tests from the batch's own notes (RAG)
  • AI tutor that can read a paused video frame
  • Comments & replies on class videos
  • Holiday-aware calendar & tasks

🏫 Run the school

  • Students & staff with virtual ID cards
  • ID-card sign-in (OCR) + one-time codes
  • Auto-attendance from meetings & videos
  • Fees & payroll — Cashfree or proof uploads
  • PTMs, broadcasts, directory, reports desk
  • Friends & live chat, groups across batches

🛡 Stay safe

  • Private AI on your GPU (or Claude)
  • Abusive-language filter → auto IP ban
  • Ban / delete on the spot (30-day restore)
  • CSP nonces, CSRF, bcrypt, lockouts, SRI
  • 40/40 scripted attack checks passing
  • Inclusive, gentle tone for special needs

📸 Screenshots

Taken in Microsoft Edge from the built-in demo school, with the local Gemma 3 1B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU.


Public website — edited with the built-in section builder
Admin dashboard — students, staff, fees, attendance and test scores at a glance

Dark mode — follows the OS, remembers your choice
A batch — students with health notes, classes, tasks and tests

AI doubt solver answering from the class notes (sources under the answer). Honest note: the small 1B model still slips — “…divide 3 by 4 and get a whole number” is wrong; see which model for which classes.

Comments & replies under a class video — ▶ 0:04 chips jump the video to that moment; teachers are labelled
Banned — signed out on the spot; the sign-in page shows the reason and the admin's contact e-mail
15 more screenshots — sign-in, calendar, AI insights, fees, IP block, deleted accounts, student & teacher views

Sign in — password, ID-card scan (OCR + one-time code) or admin
Holiday-aware calendar — every task and class in its batch colour

Students — batches, special-needs and health flags, parent contacts
AI insights — the facts come from the rules, the AI adds next steps

Fees — dues, receipts, overdue and proofs to verify
AI & services — local Gemma 3 on the GPU, OCR, e-mail, knowledge base

Student dashboard — today's classes, due work, results
Student calendar — classes, tasks and tests together

Auto-graded test with explanations
Virtual ID card — also used to sign in

Teacher dashboard — classes to start, AI insights for their batches
Teacher's batch view — attendance, scores, health notes

Teacher's watch page — answer students' questions under the video
IP block — every page and live connection from that network stops at once; reason, end time and admin e-mail shown

Deleted account — dormant for 30 days with a Restore button, then removed for good

📚 Contents

  1. Quick start
  2. Classes, subjects & batches
  3. Demo school
  4. AI models — local Gemma 3 or Claude
  5. Feature tour

  7. How the key flows work

  12. Performance & N+1 safety
