  15. CLI & maintenance
  16. Troubleshooting

🚀 Quick start

Run python app.py — or double-click start.bat on Windows (it also installs Python if it is missing). One command installs and starts everything and skips whatever is already done. (python run.py is the same launcher.)

flowchart LR
    A([▶ python app.py / start.bat]) --> B[🐍 Python + .venv<br/>+ packages]
    B --> C[🔑 .env with<br/>fresh secrets]
    C --> D[🐳 WSL2 + Docker<br/>installed & started]
    D --> E[🗄 PostgreSQL · 🔎 OCR<br/>· 📧 Mailpit]
    E --> F{GPU?}
    F -->|NVIDIA / AMD| G[🤖 Gemma 3 on vLLM<br/>in Docker]
    F -->|no| H[☁️ Claude if a key is set<br/>· fallbacks otherwise]
    G --> I([🌐 ClassNest<br/>linked to the AI])
    H --> I
Loading
# What the launcher does
1 Installs Python 3.12 with winget if Python is missing (start.bat only)
2 Creates .venv (repairs a broken one) and installs requirements.txt — only when the file changes
3 Creates .env from .env.example with fresh secrets (session key, database password, the AI container's key)
4 Installs WSL2 + Docker Desktop with winget if missing (approve the administrator prompt; Windows may need one restart)
5 Starts Docker Desktop and waits for the engine
6 docker compose up --wait → PostgreSQL + pgvector, Tesseract OCR, Mailpit
7 Finds your GPU, picks the largest Gemma 3 that fits, starts it on vLLM in Docker and links the app to it
8 Starts the web server on http://localhost:8080 (HTTPS when a certificate is configured) 
python app.py               # everything, then the web app (same as: python run.py)
python app.py --open        # ...and open the browser when it is ready (start.bat does this)
python app.py --reload      # auto-reload while developing
python app.py --setup-only  # install + start the services, not the web app
python app.py --no-llm      # don't start the local AI model even if a GPU is found
python app.py --no-docker   # use your own PostgreSQL (with pgvector) / OCR / SMTP from .env

Note

First run: ~700 MB for the database/OCR/mail containers, and — on a PC with a GPU — the vLLM image (~10 GB download, ~33 GB unpacked) plus the model weights (2 GB for Gemma 3 1B). Both download once; later starts take seconds plus 1–3 minutes for the model to load. The web app starts right away and switches its AI on by itself when the model is ready.

URL What
http://localhost:8080 🌐 Website
http://localhost:8080/login 🔑 Sign in (tabs: Student/Staff · ID card · Admin)
http://localhost:8080/admin/ai 🤖 AI & services status, with a live prompt tester
http://localhost:8025 📧 Mailpit — every email the app sends (welcome, ID cards, OTPs, warnings…)

Admin accounts come from ADMIN_USERS in .env (template: admin / ChangeMe@123, principal / ChangeMe@456). Change them — preferably to bcrypt hashes from python -m app.cli hash-password. Weak admin passwords are flagged at startup and on the dashboard.

First steps: Batches → Calendar (add national holidays) → Staff (add a teacher) → Students → Classes / Tests → check Mailpit for the ID cards. Just exploring? Load the demo school instead.

🐳 Run everything in Docker instead 
docker compose --profile app --profile llm-nvidia up -d --build   # NVIDIA GPU (use llm-amd on a ROCm Linux box)

The app container reaches the model at http://llm:8000/v1 (a network alias shared by both GPU flavours).

🔒 HTTPS for other devices (camera & microphone)

Browsers only allow camera/microphone on https:// or http://localhost. For phones/laptops on your LAN:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install cryptography
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.cli make-cert

Then set SSL_CERTFILE=certs/cert.pem, SSL_KEYFILE=certs/key.pem, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true and BASE_URL=https://<your-LAN-IP>:8080.

🏫 Classes, subjects & batches

Which classes — and up to which class?

ClassNest runs classes from Class 1 up to Class 12, and three more levels beyond school:

Level Choose it for
Class 1 – Class 12 school students — primary, middle, secondary and senior secondary. Not tied to any board or syllabus: your class notes are the syllabus the AI works from
Undergraduate college-level subjects
Competitive Exams entrance / competitive-exam coaching batches
Adult Learning courses for adults

Every batch and every student gets one of these levels in the admin forms (the list is CLASS_LEVELS in app/constants.py).

Which subjects?

Any subject. The subject is free text, so you can teach whatever you offer. The form suggests the common ones:

Mathematics · Science · Physics · Chemistry · Biology · English · Hindi · Social Studies · History · Geography · Computer Science · Accountancy · Economics · General Knowledge

The AI tutor, class notes and test generator are told the batch's class and subject (“a friendly Mathematics tutor for Class 10 students”) and answer from that batch's own class notes first.

Important

Which AI model for which classes. The 1B model that fits a 4 GB GPU explains school topics well when the class notes cover them, but it does make mistakes. In our test it said 3/4 “gives a whole number” (see the screenshot). For senior classes (9–12), competitive exams and undergraduate subjects, use a GPU with 12 GB or more (Gemma 3 4B / 12B are picked automatically) or Claude, and keep teachers reviewing AI-written tests before publishing.

Batch rules

Rule Default Setting in .env
Every batch lasts at least 1 hour MIN_BATCH_MINUTES
Active batches at most 12 MAX_BATCHES
Total batch time on any weekday 12 hours MAX_DAILY_HOURS
A student's batches may not overlap in time, and must fit the daily limit —
Nothing scheduled or due on Sunday (+ holidays from the calendar) WEEKLY_OFF_DAYS

✏️ The admin can edit everything about a batch

Admin → Batches → a batch → Edit

What How it's handled
Name, class (std), subject, colour, description saved straight away (the name must stay unique)
Days and start / end time re-checked against the batch rules and every enrolled student's other batches. An edit that would make someone's classes clash is refused, with the students' names
Teacher — the host of the batch's live classes the new teacher is notified and sees the batch at once; the previous one no longer does
Monthly fee, active / inactive inactive batches don't count towards the limits
Members Add students on the batch page (overlap-checked) or remove them with one click

Classes that are already scheduled follow the change: upcoming classes still at the old batch time move to the new time, and students are told. Upcoming live rooms hosted by the old teacher get the new one. A class you gave its own time or a substitute host keeps it. Classes that have started or ended never change.

One class at a time — Admin → Classes → a class → Edit or reschedule: change the topic, date, start/end time or the host, e.g. a substitute teacher. Holidays are respected and students are notified of a new date or time. The substitute gets the room link, sees the class on their dashboard and can start it.

🎭 Demo school

Want to see ClassNest full of life before adding real people? One command creates a realistic small tuition centre:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.cli demo-data                   # create it (36 students)
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.cli demo-data --with-insights   # ...and run the AI progress analysis too
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.cli demo-data --students 80     # more or fewer students (3-300)
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.cli demo-data --clear           # remove the demo again
What you get
👩‍🏫 14 staff principal, coordinator, five teachers (maths, science, English, physics, chemistry), a computer-science SME, counsellor, accountant, librarian, two cleaners and a security guard
🗂 8 batches Class 8 Maths & Science · Class 10 Maths, Science & English · Class 12 Physics, Chemistry & Computer Science, all within the batch rules
🧑‍🎓 36 students photos, ID proofs, virtual ID cards, parents, a few health notes and special needs, two or three batches each
📅 Classes two weeks of held classes with attendance and class notes the AI tutor answers from, plus live rooms for the next three days
📝 Work homework with submissions and grades, a weekly test per batch with graded attempts, batch-chat messages
🎬 Class video a short “Rational numbers” clip on the Class 10 Maths class, with a comment thread (a question pinned to 0:04, the teacher's answers and students' replies)
💰 Money two months of fees (paid, pending and overdue) and last month's salaries
📨 Website three contact enquiries

Every demo account signs in with the password Demo@12345, for example diya.fernandes (student), sunita.rao (teacher), meera.iyer (principal) or ramesh.yadav (cleaner). The command prints more.

Caution

Remove the demo (--clear) before real use — everyone can read its password here. --clear removes the demo people, batches and enquiries with everything attached to them (classes, fees, attendance…), including demo batches you edited, so don't put real students into demo batches. Demo e-mail addresses use the reserved demo.classnest.test domain, so nothing reaches real people. --with-insights does send its summary to your ADMIN_ALERT_EMAILS.

🤖 AI models — local Gemma 3 or Claude

ClassNest talks to one AI backend at a time, chosen by AI_PROVIDER in .env:

AI_PROVIDER Uses Privacy Cost
auto (default) Gemma 3 on this PC's GPU when one is found → otherwise Claude if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set → otherwise the built-in fallbacks ✅ local first free locally
local Always the bundled vLLM container ✅ never leaves the PC free
anthropic Claude through the Anthropic API data sent to Anthropic pay per use
openai Any OpenAI-compatible server in OPENAI_BASE_URL (Ollama, LM Studio, another vLLM…) depends depends
off No AI — every feature uses its deterministic fallback ✅ free 
flowchart LR
    APP[⚡ ClassNest] -->|OpenAI-compatible API<br/>Bearer key| VLLM
    APP -.->|Anthropic SDK<br/>when AI_PROVIDER=anthropic| CLAUDE[☁️ Claude API]
    subgraph Docker["🐳 Docker"]
        VLLM[vLLM server<br/>127.0.0.1:8002 · alias llm:8000]
        VLLM --> GPU[(🎮 NVIDIA / AMD GPU<br/>Gemma 3 weights)]
    end
Loading

🎮 Local: Gemma 3 on vLLM, in Docker

run.py reads the GPU's memory and picks the model automatically (override with VLLM_MODEL):

GPU memory Model Context Images
4 – 11.5 GB gemma-3-1b-it 8K — (OCR text is used instead)
11.5 – 15.5 GB gemma-3-4b-it 8K ✅
15.5 – 31 GB gemma-3-4b-it 16K ✅
31 – 46 GB gemma-3-12b-it 8K ✅
46 GB + gemma-3-12b-it 16K ✅
NVIDIA AMD
Works on Windows (Docker Desktop + WSL2) and Linux Linux with ROCm (Docker Desktop on Windows can't pass AMD GPUs to containers)
Compose profile llm-nvidia → vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 llm-amd → rocm/vllm RDNA build (Radeon RX 7000/9000); set VLLM_AMD_IMAGE=rocm/vllm:latest for Instinct
Needs a recent NVIDIA driver (the container toolkit ships with Docker Desktop) /dev/kfd, /dev/dri (ROCm kernel driver)

What the launcher takes care of:

  • Memory sizing — vLLM is given what is really free inside the container (the CUDA runtime and WSL take ~0.7 GB on Windows), capped at 90 %; GPUs under 6 GB skip CUDA-graph capture to save memory.
  • Linking — exports OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1 (host port VLLM_PORT, so 8000 stays free for the web app), the per-install key and the model name to the app, and matches the app's AI concurrency to vLLM's batch size (vLLM batches requests itself).
  • Restarts — a healthy container is left alone; a failing one, or one serving another model, is replaced.
  • Weights are cached in the hf-cache Docker volume. The unsloth/gemma-3-* repos are ungated copies of Google's Gemma 3 weights under the same Gemma licence; to use google/gemma-3-* set VLLM_MODEL and HF_TOKEN.
  • The port is bound to 127.0.0.1 only and every request needs the key.

Tip

Measured on a 4 GB RTX 3050 laptop GPU (Gemma 3 1B): first token in ~0.2 s when idle, ~122 tokens/s across 12 parallel requests, room for ~49,800 tokens of context (six full 8K conversations at once). Answers are friendly and fast, but a 1B model makes factual slips — generated tests are always labelled “review before publishing”. A 12 GB+ GPU (Gemma 3 4B) or Claude gives much better accuracy.

Because small models slip, ClassNest keeps the facts out of the model's hands where it matters. Tutor answers are grounded in the batch's class notes. Progress alerts state the numbers from the rules, so the AI only writes the next steps and the note to parents, and any AI text that quotes figures or leaves placeholders is replaced. Prompt scaffolding the model echoes back (<context>, [1] Class notes…, Question: …) is stripped from answers.

☁️ Claude, when you don't want to run the model locally

  1. Create an API key at https://platform.claude.com.
  2. In .env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... and AI_PROVIDER=anthropic (or leave auto on a PC without a GPU).
  3. Restart. Admin → AI & services shows the model, effort and context window.
Setting Default Notes
ANTHROPIC_MODEL claude-opus-5-5 claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-haiku-5-5 are cheaper and faster (Nov 2026 list prices per million tokens in/out: Opus 5.5 $4/$20 · Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 · Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50)
ANTHROPIC_EFFORT medium low = quicker, cheaper answers; high = more careful reasoning
ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS 16000 room for the model's (hidden) thinking plus the answer

How it is wired (app/services/ai_claude.py, official anthropic SDK): every request streams; tests and grading use structured outputs (JSON Schema), so answers always have the right shape; refusal fallbacks are switched on (fallbacks: "default") so a request the safety filter declines is retried server-side on Anthropic's recommended model — and if the whole chain declines, the feature falls back (the doubt goes to the teacher). Claude has no embeddings endpoint, so knowledge search uses the built-in lexical vectors.

✨ Feature tour

🌐 Public website — edited like WordPress
🧱 Section builder Hero, feature grid, stats, “how it works”, testimonials, FAQ, gallery, rich text, call-to-action and contact sections. Drag to reorder, show/hide, edit with a rich-text editor (Quill) and image uploads.
🎨 Branding Institute name, tagline, logo, primary/accent colours, footer, social links.
📞 Contact Your school's email, WhatsApp and phone come from .env (CONTACT_EMAIL, CONTACT_WHATSAPP, CONTACT_PHONE) and can be overridden in Branding. Floating WhatsApp button, contact form with honeypot + rate limiting.
📄 Pages Terms & Conditions (with the disclaimer), Privacy, About — or any page you create.

👩‍🏫 Academics
🗂 Batches Class 1–12, Undergraduate, Competitive Exams or Adult Learning, any subject. Each batch ≥ 1 hour, at most 12 active batches, at most 12 hours/day cumulative (per weekday meter). Students can't join overlapping batches. Name, class, subject, days, times, teacher and members are all editable by the admin, and scheduled classes follow.
🗓 Holiday-aware calendar Holidays block assignment dates and deadlines. Vacations (e.g. May summer break) allow holiday homework only. Weekly offs (Sunday by default). One-click national holidays + summer vacation preset. Date fields show live hints (“⛔ Diwali — not allowed”).
✅ Task-based scheduling Assignments, homework, projects and tests appear on each student's calendar. Submissions (text + file), late flag, grading & feedback.
🎥 Classes Each class uses either a pre-recorded video (no meeting needed) or a live class. Without a video, a live meeting is mandatory — a room is created and admins are warned by SMTP email (on scheduling, 24 h before, and if it hasn't started 15 min after the start time). Any class can be rescheduled or given a substitute host until it starts.
💬 Video comments Under every class video and recording: comments with replies (a reply to a reply stays in the thread), optional “pin to this moment” timestamps that jump the video there, Teacher / Admin labels, live updates without reloading. Only the batch, its teacher and admins can see them. Replies notify the person answered; a student's comment notifies the teacher. Abusive words are filtered like the chats, and authors or teachers can delete.
🧪 AI tests The AI writes MCQ / true-false / short-answer questions from the batch's class & subject and the knowledge base (pgvector RAG), constrained to an exact JSON schema. Edit everything, publish to a batch (holiday rules apply), timed test with autosave, auto-grading, AI grading of short answers, question analytics, CSV export.
🧠 Knowledge base Upload notes, PDFs or images (OCR'd). Class notes and video notes are indexed automatically. Hybrid lexical + semantic search with reciprocal-rank fusion.

🎙 Live classes (Google-Meet-style, inside the app)
📹 WebRTC HD video grid, mute/camera, screen sharing, chat, hand-raise, reactions, speaking indicators, participant list, host mute/remove, auto-reconnect.
⏺ Recording The host's browser records a composite of every tile + mixed audio and uploads it in 5-second chunks. It becomes a video for students who missed the class.
📝 AI notes Live captions + chat form the transcript; the AI writes structured notes (summary, key concepts, examples, Q&A, homework).
🙋 Auto-attendance Present if the student attends the whole meeting (MEETING_ATTENDANCE_RATIO, default 90% to tolerate network blips) or watches ≥ 50% of the video/recording (unique seconds watched, anti-skip; the video length comes from the server, never the student's browser).

🤖 AI everywhere
💬 AI doubt solver Per-lesson and per-batch tutor that answers from the class's own notes, streamed live. 📸 Ask about this moment: screenshots the paused video frame + timestamp — vision models read the image; OCR text from the frame and the transcript at that moment are added too.
🧑‍💼 Private AI assistant Live chat that remembers context (rolling memory) and is visible only to the user. Staff can ask about a student's progress (real attendance/score data for their batches); students ask what's due or how they're doing.
🛡 Concerns → reports If a student complains about a staff member (or anyone raises bullying / harassment / safety), only that message is logged to the admin Reports desk: dismiss · accept · resolve · ban. The reporter gets notified of the outcome.
📈 Performance monitor Daily analysis of scores, attendance and missed work → alerts to admins (digest), batch teachers (digest + in-app) and parents (polite email).
💛 Inclusive tone Students flagged with special needs / health issues get lenient thresholds and gentle, patient wording everywhere — except formal warnings.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 People, onboarding & community
🪪 Registration Photo (upload or webcam), date of birth, contact details and ID proof are mandatory. Staff roles: teacher, principal, vice-principal, coordinator, SME, counsellor, accountant, librarian, lab assistant, receptionist, cleaner, security, driver…
📧 Welcome emails New joiners get a thank-you email (parent in CC) and a confidential email with their virtual ID card (inline + PNG) and password.
🔑 Sign-in Username/password, or scan the ID card → Tesseract OCR → one-time code to email and phone. Admins sign in with the accounts in .env.
🚪 Remove · ban · delete Every action takes effect on the spot: sessions end and live classes and chats close. Remove withdraws access with a stated reason (templates: spamming, bad behaviour, fee default…); reinstate any time. Ban keeps the account and its data but shows the person as Banned everywhere; their sign-in page says banned, gives the reason and the admin's contact e-mail. You can also block their network. Delete puts the account dormant for 30 days: hidden, shown as “Deleted user”, restorable with one click. After that it is removed for good automatically, files included. Comments others replied to stay as placeholders.
🏥 Health records Conditions, medication, emergency contacts — visible to the student's batch teachers.
👫 Friends & live chat Friend requests, unfriend, block, live direct messages over WebSockets (typing indicator, unread counts, toasts), groups with classmates and teachers from any batch, report button. Conversations with a banned or deleted person become read-only.
💬 Batch chats Live group chat per batch with moderator deletion.

💰 Finance
🧾 Fees Monthly dues per batch, receipts, statements, CSV. If Cashfree is set up: students pay online and fees reflect automatically (webhook + server-side verification). If not: students upload a payment screenshot → the office verifies or rejects with a reason.
💼 Salaries Payments for every staff role. Cashfree Payouts (bank / UPI) reflect automatically; otherwise the salary receipt / proof upload is mandatory. Staff download receipts and printable slips.

📣 Communication
✉️ Broadcasts Email (and optional SMS) to all students, all parents, batch students/parents, staff by role or extra addresses; formal templates; AI polish.
👪 PTMs Formal invitations, RSVP tracking without login, online/hybrid video room with guest access, reminders and cancellations.
📇 Directory One-click email, call and WhatsApp for students, parents and staff.

🎨 Experience

Premium MDB-based design system, light & dark mode (remembers your choice, follows the OS by default), smooth page progress bar, toasts, accessible charts with a table view, minified + fingerprinted CSS/JS with long-lived caching. A feather-in-a-nest favicon (SVG + PNG + .ico + Apple touch icon) and an installable web-app manifest that switch to your own logo and colours once you set them in Branding.

🏗 Architecture

flowchart LR
    subgraph Browser["🧑‍🎓 Browser · Jinja + MDB + vanilla JS"]
        UI[Pages & dashboards]
        RTC[WebRTC live class]
        WS[WebSockets: meet · batch chat · friends]
    end

What the numbers say

  • Up to 200 people at once, ClassNest barely notices: median ~20 ms, p95 at most 52 ms, the worker less than half busy.
  • 300 is comfortable: p95 0.47 s.
  • At 400, one worker is full. It levels off at ~92 requests a second and pages slow to a median of 0.63 s (p95 1.1 s), but nothing failed. The slowest of all 31,900 requests took 2.4 s. ClassNest runs a single worker by design (live classes and chats keep their rooms in memory), so that is this laptop's ceiling; a faster CPU core raises it.
  • The database is never the bottleneck: about a third of a core at 300–400 people (peak 54 %).
  • Memory stays small: the app process grew from 192 MB to 255 MB; the database never passed 332 MB.
  • The AI kept answering: all 82 questions were answered by the model itself, with no fallbacks. The first word came in 0.2 s at 50 people and 1.6 s at 400. The 8 askers loaded the GPU equally in every step, so that slowdown comes from the busy app worker, not from the GPU. Whole answers: median 12 s, p95 39 s.
  • Sign-in is slow on purpose (median 0.25 s): bcrypt makes guessing stolen passwords expensive. The CPU spikes at the start of each step are the new arrivals signing in.

Note

Simulated people are much busier than real ones. Each clicks every 2–6 seconds for ten minutes straight; real students read, watch and write for far longer between clicks. Locust ran on the same laptop and never reported running short of CPU. Not covered by this test: downloading the video files themselves (the watch page and progress tracking were tested), and the WebSockets of live classes and chats (live-class video is peer-to-peer).

What the load test found — and fixed
Found Fix
The first full run lost 73 of about 31,500 requests (0.23 %) to connection reset / remote end closed connection, all at 300–400 people, with nothing in the server log. None of the 3,600+ requests sent straight after another response (sign-in, calendar feed, video progress) failed. uvicorn closes an idle connection after 5 s by default; on a busy worker that close can land just as the next request is sent on it. Connections now stay open 75 s (KEEP_ALIVE_SECONDS), longer than the 30-second notification poll. Same load again: 0 failures.
The report would have counted the AI tutor's streamed answers (12–39 s) as requests, inflating p99 and "slowest" AI timings are logged separately; the request tables hold only page and API calls
A rate-limited comment was counted twice Counted once, under its own name
Once moved into loadtest/, the resource sampler measured the AI container instead of the database It locates the project explicitly and stops if the database container isn't found

⚡ Performance & N+1 safety

  • Every ORM relationship is lazy="raise" — an accidental lazy load fails loudly instead of silently issuing N queries. Lists use selectinload / joinedload.
  • Measured, not assumed. A test-only wrapper counted every SQL statement per request while every role crawled every page: 405 requests across 82 page types.
    • No statement ever repeated more than 5 times in one request (the N+1 signature).
    • The heaviest page (the student dashboard) runs 12 statements, and list pages run the same 5 whether they show 3 rows or 25.
    • The write paths that looped are now batched: adding students to a batch (was 2 queries per student, now 6 in total for 12 students), the timetable clash check (was 2 per enrolled student, now 14 in total for 17), and the end-of-class attendance update (was 1 per participant, now 1 statement).
  • First-come-first-served database pool (app/database.py) — no request can be starved by newcomers, so bursts never approach the 30 s pool timeout.
  • Connections are reused for 75 s (KEEP_ALIVE_SECONDS), longer than the 30-second notification poll. Open pages keep one connection instead of reconnecting on every poll. With uvicorn's 5-second default, a busy server sometimes closed a connection just as the next request arrived (found by the load test).
  • Dashboards use one round-trip of scalar sub-queries and grouped aggregates; the performance monitor uses a fixed number of GROUP BY queries regardless of student count.
  • Notifications, fee dues and attendance are written with bulk / multi-row inserts and ON CONFLICT upserts.
  • The local model batches requests (vLLM continuous batching); the app sends up to vLLM's batch size at once.
  • CSS/JS are minified (rcssmin / rjsmin) and fingerprinted at startup and served with Cache-Control: immutable; GZip for responses; WebRTC media is peer-to-peer.
  • Background jobs run under a Postgres advisory lock, so only one worker runs them.

Load test: the 10-minute Locust run in loadtest/README.md (always against a copy of the database).

Tables are created automatically on startup (CREATE EXTENSION vector + create_all). If you change EMBEDDING_DIM later, drop the knowledge_chunks table and use Knowledge base → Re-index all.

🩺 Troubleshooting

Symptom Fix
Could not connect to PostgreSQL Start with python app.py / start.bat (it starts Docker and the database); check POSTGRES_PORT isn't used by another Postgres
Port … is already in use Another program (or a second ClassNest) has it: close that, or set PORT and BASE_URL in .env. The local AI model sits on 8002 (VLLM_PORT); the launcher moves it there by itself
Launcher says Windows must restart WSL2 was just enabled — restart once. If it repeats, enable SVM / Intel VT-x virtualization in the BIOS
AI features say “offline” Open Admin → AI & services. Local model still loading? It takes 1–3 minutes after each start (docker compose --profile llm-nvidia logs -f llm-nvidia)
vLLM log: Free memory on device … is less than desired GPU memory utilization Close other GPU apps (games, browsers with hardware acceleration) or set VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.6 in .env
No GPU found / AMD GPU on Windows vLLM needs NVIDIA on Windows (or AMD on Linux + ROCm) — use AI_PROVIDER=anthropic with a Claude key instead
Claude: API key was rejected Check ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (and that AI_PROVIDER=anthropic or auto), then restart
Camera/mic blocked Use https:// (see Quick start) or http://localhost
No emails Open Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) or check Admin → Email log for SMTP errors
ID-card sign-in fails Start the OCR container (docker compose up -d ocr); use a sharp, well-lit photo or the PNG from the email
Too many failed sign-in attempts Wait 15 minutes (ACCOUNT_LOCK_MINUTES) or restart the app
Someone got auto-banned on a shared network Bans are per IP — lift it in Admin → Security and consider a shorter ABUSE_BAN_HOURS
Behind nginx / Caddy: now and then a 502 Bad Gateway The proxy reused a connection the app had just closed. Set KEEP_ALIVE_SECONDS longer than the proxy's upstream idle timeout (nginx keepalive_timeout 60 s, Caddy 2 min)
A person says they are banned / their account was deleted Admin → Students/Staff → (status: Banned / Deleted) → the person → Unban / Restore. A deleted account can be restored for DELETED_RETENTION_DAYS (30); after that it's gone for good

1445524179.readme_html:
📇 CardVault

Snap a visiting card. Get a clean, searchable contact.

A local visiting-card scanner: OpenCV straightens the photo, Apple Vision (optional) reads the text, Gemma 3 turns it into a contact, and PostgreSQL + pgvector make it searchable.

Warning

Student-grade project. Use at your own risk. CardVault was built for learning and is provided "as is", without any warranty. Its authors and contributors are not liable for any damage, data loss, wrong contact details or other problems arising from its use. Always double-check what it reads. See the full Disclaimer.

📚 Contents

  • ✨ Features
  • 📸 Screenshots
  • 🧭 How it works
  • 🚀 Quick start
  • 🖱️ Using CardVault
  • 🔤 Text reading: Apple Vision or Gemma only
  • 📤 Export formats
  • 🔌 JSON API
  • ⚙️ Configuration
  • 🔐 Local-only by design
  • 🗂️ Project layout
  • 🧪 Tests
  • 🛠️ Troubleshooting
  • ⚠️ Disclaimer

✨ Features
📷 Any photo works Drag and drop, choose files, or use the webcam. JPG, PNG, WEBP and iPhone HEIC are supported, and several cards can be scanned at once.
🧹 OpenCV clean-up Finds the card in the photo, corrects the perspective, evens out shadows, denoises and sharpens. Sideways cards are turned upright.
🤖 Gemma understands it Name, title, company, phones with their type (mobile / work / fax…), emails, websites, address split into city / state / PIN, plus an industry and search tags.
🔤 OCR is optional Apple Vision reads the text first (fast, offline, macOS). Untick it and Gemma reads the image on its own.
📝 Review before saving Each card shows the straightened image next to editable fields. Duplicates are flagged. The queue survives restarts.
🔎 Smart search Matches exact words, typos (priyaa sharmaa), part of a phone number (98765) and meaning ("interior designer in Pune", via pgvector). ✨ Gemma can expand vague queries ("someone who builds apps").
⬇️ Export anything Excel, CSV, vCard (straight into your phone), raw OCR text, or JSON, for all contacts or just your search results.
🏠 Stays on your machines Contacts live in your own PostgreSQL. Photos only go to your own Gemma gateway on your network.

📸 Screenshots


Scan: drop photos, choose whether Apple Vision reads the text first
Review: straightened card next to the fields Gemma filled in

Contacts: search, edit, vCard, export
Smart search: Gemma expands "someone who builds apps"

The screenshots use the generated sample cards in samples/. These are not real people.

🧭 How it works

flowchart LR
    A["📷 Card photo"] --> B["🧹 OpenCV<br/>find · straighten · clean"]
    B --> C{"🔤 Apple Vision OCR<br/>(optional)"}
    C -- "text + layout" --> D["🤖 Gemma 3 12B<br/>reads text + image"]
    C -. "switched off" .-> D
    D --> E["📝 Review & edit"]
    E --> F[("🐘 PostgreSQL<br/>+ pgvector")]
    F --> G["🔎 Hybrid search"]
    F --> H["⬇️ Excel · CSV · vCard<br/>OCR text · JSON"]
Loading
Step Technology What it does
1 OpenCV Detects the card outline, warps it flat, flattens the lighting (CLAHE), denoises and sharpens.
2 Apple Vision (optional) Reads every line with its position and size. Takes about 0.3 s, works offline, and handles sideways or upside-down cards.
3 Gemma 3 via your OpenAI-compatible gateway Receives the OCR text and the card image, and returns schema-checked JSON. If Gemma is offline, a rule-based parser takes over.
4 FastAPI + Jinja2 Server-rendered pages. Cards are processed in background workers and appear live on the Review page.
5 PostgreSQL + pgvector Stores contacts, card images and the review queue. Search combines keywords, pg_trgm typo matching and vector similarity (HNSW index).

🚀 Quick start

You need: macOS, Python 3 (developed and tested on 3.15), and PostgreSQL. The setup script compiles and installs pgvector for you. You also need a Gemma model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a gateway.

./setup.sh        # venv + packages + pgvector + database   (same as: make setup)
./run.sh          # starts http://localhost:10000 and opens your browser   (same as: make run)

You can also start the FastAPI file directly, for example with your editor's ▶ Run button (select the .venv interpreter):

.venv/bin/python webapp/main.py     # or: .venv/bin/python -m webapp.main
Command What it does
make check Is PostgreSQL / pgvector / Gemma / OCR / embeddings working?
make test Runs the test suite on throw-away databases (your contacts are never touched).
make dev Auto-reload while you edit the code.
make samples Regenerates the sample card photos in samples/.

🖱️ Using CardVault

  1. 📤 Scan (/scan): drop photos, click to choose them, or capture with the webcam. Choose your options, then press Scan.
    • ☑️ Read the text with Apple Vision first: on by default (see below).
    • ☐ Save straight away: skip review for cards that aren't possible duplicates.
  2. 📝 Review (/review): cards are read in the background, 3 at a time, and each one appears when it's ready. Fix anything, then Save or Save all ready. Possible duplicates (same email, phone or name) are flagged.
  3. 📇 Contacts (/contacts): search, sort, edit, delete, or download a single vCard.
  4. ⬇️ Export: pick a format and click Download. It exports exactly what's on screen.

🔤 Text reading: Apple Vision or Gemma only

Apple Vision is optional. Gemma 3 is a vision model and can read the card image on its own.

Apple Vision + Gemma (default on a Mac) Gemma only
Speed (per card, Gemma 3 12B) ~9 s ~11–13 s
Accuracy on the sample cards all fields correct all fields correct
Works when Gemma is offline ✅ rule-based fallback ❌ nothing can read the card
Needs macOS yes no
Raw "OCR text" export from Apple Vision Gemma's transcription

There are three ways to choose:

  • Per scan: the Read the text with Apple Vision first checkbox on the Scan page.
  • Always off: set OCR_ENGINE=none in .env.
  • From scripts: add ocr=false to /api/scan.

OpenCV clean-up happens either way.

📤 Export formats

Format Best for
📊 Excel (.xlsx) Spreadsheets: one row per contact, filters, frozen header
🧾 CSV (.csv) Google Sheets, CRMs, any import. UTF-8 with BOM, protected against formula injection
📱 vCard (.vcf) Importing straight into iPhone / Android / Google / Outlook contacts
🔤 OCR text (.txt) The raw text read from each card
🧑‍💻 JSON (.json) Everything, for developers

🔌 JSON API

Interactive documentation is at http://localhost:10000/docs.

curl -F files=@card.jpg "http://localhost:10000/api/scan?save=true"            # scan now (+ save)
curl -F files=@card.jpg "http://localhost:10000/api/scan?ocr=false"            # Gemma reads the image alone
curl "http://localhost:10000/api/contacts?q=interior+designer+pune"            # hybrid search
curl "http://localhost:10000/api/contacts?q=someone+who+builds+apps&smart=true" # with Gemma keywords
curl http://localhost:10000/api/status
All endpoints
Method Path
POST /api/scan Scan photos synchronously (save, ocr query flags)
GET /api/contacts List or search contacts (q, smart, sort, limit)
GET /api/contacts/{id} One contact
GET /api/scans, /api/scans/{id} Review queue
GET /api/status Database, Gemma, OCR and embedding status
GET /contacts/export?fmt=xlsx|csv|vcf|txt|json&q=… Download
GET /contacts/{id}/vcard One vCard

⚙️ Configuration

Everything lives in .env. .env.example is a template.

Variable Default Meaning
DATABASE_URL – PostgreSQL connection. The cardvault database is created automatically.
LLM_BASE_URL / LLM_API_KEY / LLM_MODEL – / – / gemma Any OpenAI-compatible server, for example your gateway http://192.168.0.226:8000/v1, or Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 with model gemma3:12b.
LLM_SEND_IMAGE true Also send the card image to Gemma. Switched off automatically for text-only models.
OCR_ENGINE auto auto = Apple Vision on macOS, none = Gemma reads the image alone.
EMBED_PROVIDER auto auto, openai, local (model2vec) or hashing
EMBED_MODEL / EMBED_BASE_URL – An embeddings endpoint, e.g. embeddinggemma. Your gateway doesn't serve one, so vectors are made locally.
LOCAL_EMBED_MODEL minishlab/potion-base-8M Local model2vec model: 256 dimensions, CPU only, about 30 MB, downloaded once.
DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION IN Country used for phone numbers printed without a country code
SCAN_WORKERS 3 Cards processed in parallel
ALLOWED_HOSTS localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 Host names the app answers to (see below)
HOST / PORT 127.0.0.1 / 10000 Where the web server listens
🐘 How pgvector was installed without sudo

The EDB PostgreSQL 18 installer keeps its extension folders root-owned. So scripts/install_pgvector.sh compiles pgvector 0.8.7 and installs it into /Users/Shared/pgvector/pg18, which the postgres service can read. scripts/setup_db.py then registers that folder with PostgreSQL 18:

ALTER SYSTEM SET extension_control_path = '$system:/Users/Shared/pgvector/pg18/share';
ALTER SYSTEM SET dynamic_library_path   = '$libdir:/Users/Shared/pgvector/pg18/lib';
SELECT pg_reload_conf();

To undo this:

  1. Drop the cardvault database.
  2. Run ALTER SYSTEM RESET extension_control_path; ALTER SYSTEM RESET dynamic_library_path; SELECT pg_reload_conf();
  3. Delete /Users/Shared/pgvector.

For a conventional install instead: sudo make -C .build/pgvector-v0.8.7 PG_CONFIG=/Library/PostgreSQL/18/bin/pg_config install

If the embedding model that made your vectors is temporarily unavailable, semantic search pauses instead of throwing the vectors away. The sidebar then shows Search vectors paused.

🔐 Local-only by design

CardVault has no login, so it protects itself in other ways:

  • It only answers to the host names in ALLOWED_HOSTS, which blocks DNS-rebinding tricks.
  • It rejects form posts coming from other websites, so a malicious page can't delete your contacts.

To use it from your phone on the same Wi-Fi, run HOST=0.0.0.0 ./run.sh and add your Mac's IP (e.g. 192.168.0.185) to ALLOWED_HOSTS. Be aware that anyone on that network can then open it.

🗂️ Project layout

webapp/                    FastAPI + Jinja2 web app
├── main.py                routes, downloads, JSON API, `python webapp/main.py`
├── services.py            shared objects, background scan workers, status cache
├── forms.py               HTML form ⇄ Contact
├── templates/             base, scan, review, contacts, edit (+ partials)
└── static/                style.css, app.js (drag & drop, webcam, live review)
cardscan/                  the scanning engine (no web code)
├── imaging.py             OpenCV: decode (HEIC/EXIF), card detection, perspective warp, enhancement
├── ocr.py                 Apple Vision OCR, reading order, orientation fix
├── llm.py                 Gemma client: JSON-schema extraction, fallbacks, smart-search keywords
├── contact.py             Contact model, phone/email/URL normalisation, rule-based fallback
├── embeddings.py          model2vec / OpenAI-compatible / hashing embedders
├── db.py                  PostgreSQL + pgvector: contacts, review queue, duplicates, hybrid search
├── exporters.py           Excel, CSV, vCard 3.0, OCR text, JSON
└── pipeline.py            photo → contact
scripts/                   setup_db.py, install_pgvector.sh, check.py, make_sample_cards.py
tests/                     67 tests
docs/screenshots/          images used in this README

🧪 Tests

make test        # 67 tests, ~15 s

The tests cover:

  • OpenCV card detection and Apple Vision OCR in all 4 orientations
  • phone, email and URL parsing
  • every export format
  • the Gemma client against fake servers, including fallbacks and races
  • pgvector hybrid search
  • the full web flow: upload → review → save → search → edit → export
  • the security checks

They run on throw-away databases and switch Gemma off, so they are fast and never touch your contacts.

🛠️ Troubleshooting

Problem Fix
🔴 Gemma offline in the sidebar Run make check, then click Re-check. Check LLM_API_KEY. Until it's back, cards are parsed with rules, so review them carefully.
CardVault can't start page Fix DATABASE_URL in .env, start PostgreSQL, run make setup, then reload.
Port 10000 is busy Another copy is running. Stop it, or use PORT=10010 ./run.sh.
Unknown host Open http://localhost:10000, or add the name or IP you used to ALLOWED_HOSTS.
Search vectors paused The embedding model can't be reached. Keyword search still works, and vectors are filled in when it's back.
Search misses someone Try part of the phone number or email, or tick ✨ Smart search. After changing embedding settings, click Re-index.
A field is wrong That's expected now and then with OCR and AI. Fix it on the Review page or with ✏️ Edit.

⚠️ Disclaimer

CardVault is a student-grade project built for learning and demonstration. It is not a commercial product, has not been professionally audited, and is not intended for production or business-critical use.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NON-INFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS, CONTRIBUTORS OR ANYONE ELSE INVOLVED BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES, DATA LOSS OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR ITS USE.

In plain words:

  • 🧐 Check the results. OCR and AI can misread names, numbers and emails. Verify a contact before you rely on it.
  • 🔓 Keep it private. There is no login or user management, and no security audit has been done. Keep it on your own computer or trusted network.
  • 🪪 Respect people's data. Visiting cards contain personal data. You are responsible for how you collect, store and share it, and for following the privacy laws that apply to you (e.g. India's DPDP Act 2023, GDPR).
  • 💾 Back up what matters. Export your contacts regularly. Nobody is responsible if data is lost.
  • 📦 Third-party parts (Gemma, OpenCV, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Apple Vision, FastAPI, model2vec…) are covered by their own licences and terms of use.

Takes about 0.3 s, works offline, and handles sideways or upside-down cards. | | 3 | **Gemma 3** via your OpenAI-compatible gateway | Receives the OCR text **and** the card image, and returns schema-checked JSON. If Gemma is offline, a rule-based parser takes over. | | 4 | **FastAPI + Jinja2** | Server-rendered pages. Cards are processed in background workers and appear live on the Review page. | | 5 | **PostgreSQL + pgvector** | Stores contacts, card images and the review queue. Search combines keywords, `pg_trgm` typo matching and vector similarity (HNSW index). | ## 🚀 Quick start **You need:** macOS, Python 3 (developed and tested on 3.15), and PostgreSQL. The setup script compiles and installs pgvector for you. You also need a Gemma model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a gateway. ```bash ./setup.sh # venv + packages + pgvector + database (same as: make setup) ./run.sh # starts http://localhost:10000 and opens your browser (same as: make run) ``` You can also start the FastAPI file directly, for example with your editor's **▶ Run** button (select the `.venv` interpreter): ```bash .venv/bin/python webapp/main.py # or: .venv/

1440901640.readme_html:
Hiring, attendance, payroll, tasks, video meetings, chats and a marketplace in one app.
It runs on your own machine, with a local AI so company data stays there, or Claude if you switch it on with your own key.

Quick start  ·  What it does  ·  AI, IDs, payments  ·  Load test  ·  How it fits together  ·  Security  ·  License

Important

A student project, free to use under the MIT license. It hasn't been audited or certified and comes with no warranty, so check it carefully before relying on it. See the license.

A company's dashboard Chats, one click away on every page

The people and the company in these screenshots are made up.

⚡ Quick start

You need Windows 11 and an internet connection. Everything else installs itself.

git clone <this repository's URL> deminic

Then open the deminic folder and double-click start.cmd.

Your browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:8000 when the app is ready. Close the start.cmd window to stop the app, and double-click it again to start it back up.

Tip

Running python app.py, such as with VS Code's Run button, does the same thing, even with the wrong Python selected.

What one click sets up

Step What happens
🐍 Python and packages Installs uv and Python 3.15 with winget, then the app's packages. A working environment is left alone.
🔑 .env Makes it from .env.example with its own random passwords, and picks your graphics card. An existing .env is never changed.
📁 Folders Creates uploads, logs, backups and the built-assets folder.
🐳 WSL and Docker Desktop Installs them if they're missing. Windows asks for permission, and WSL needs one restart: double-click start.cmd again afterwards.
🗄️ Redis, ClamAV, PostgreSQL Starts them in containers. The app waits for these three.
🧠 vLLM, Whisper, LibreTranslate Sets them up in a second, minimized window. The app doesn't wait: their buttons turn on once they're ready.

Good to know

  • First run: ClamAV downloads its virus database, and the AI's image and model are very large, so the AI can take a long time to appear. After each reboot it takes about 4 minutes to start.
  • The local AI needs an AMD or NVIDIA graphics card with about 16 GB of memory, a current driver, and about 60 GB of free disk space. Without those, the app runs with its AI buttons turned off.
  • Sign-up codes: until you set up SMTP and Twilio, they're printed in the start.cmd window.
  • Maps: creating a company needs a free Geoapify key in .env.
  • Admin console: it stays off until you set ADMIN_USERNAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env. It's also where you switch the AI, ID checks and payments, and paste their keys.
  • Use git clone, not a ZIP. Windows treats files from a ZIP as downloaded from the internet and may refuse to run start.cmd.

✨ What it does

👥 People and companies

  • Sign-up with email and SMS codes, and an 18+ check
  • Positions, joining and leaving approvals, and job offers
  • Requests nobody answers in 30 days are declined by the system, which says so
  • An ID checker for people and companies from any country, shown as a badge, that can be switched off
  • An employee limit each company sets, which only its owner and co-owners can see
  • Company search by meaning, CV reading and an AI company finder
  • Single company mode, where the whole site runs for one company and the home page says so, with a button to it

🗂️ Work

  • Tasks with deadlines, where the AI can pick up to 5 people
  • A calendar with tasks, meetings, holidays and attendance
  • Attendance counted only inside working hours, with idle detection and a month view
  • Working hours that can change once every 30 days
  • Leave requests and colleague reviews

💰 Pay

  • Salary cycles and payslips
  • Payments recorded in any currency at the day's rate
  • A payroll guard that warns a company, then halts it, if it owes staff more than it has
  • A company halts if its owner isn't online for 7 days in a row, alerts everyone, and resumes when they're back
  • Salary money never moves through the app: companies pay from their own bank and record it here

💬 Talk

  • Company and personal chats with files, and a profile one click from any name
  • Video meetings with screen sharing, recording, live English captions, AI notes and a theme switch mid-call
  • Deminic AI, an assistant that streams answers, reads pictures and can search the web
  • Nine languages: English, Hindi, Arabic, German, French, Dutch, Spanish, Italian and Chinese

🤖 Company AI

  • A promotion review that can be off, suggest people, or promote by itself
  • "Who's best for this task?", ranked from CVs, reviews and work history
  • Growth reviews for profiles and companies
  • One switch for every AI feature: local (vLLM) or online (Claude, with your own key)

🛒 Shop

  • Storefront, search, cart and checkout, with one switch: off, cash on delivery only, test payments, or Cashfree
  • Order tracking, delivery codes, returns and buyer reviews
  • An AI shopping assistant, review summaries, competitor price tracking and AI-assigned shop tasks

🔌 AI, ID checks and payments

All three are switched in the admin console, under services. Paste a key there with your admin password and it's tried for real, saved to .env only if it works, and never shown again. No restart needed.

Choices What's free Keys
🧠 AI Local: vLLM with Gemma 3 12B on your graphics card.
Online: Claude.		 Local is free. Claude is paid per use by your key. Anthropic API key
🪪 ID checker Off: format and check digit only, nothing is sent anywhere.
On: every check below that's set up.		 See below. Didit and Companies House are optional
💳 Payments Off: no orders at all.
COD: cash on delivery only.
Test: pretend payments.
Online: Cashfree.		 No gateway is free per payment. Cashfree has no setup or monthly fee, about 1.95% + GST a payment. Cashfree payment keys

What the ID checker covers

ID Check Cost
Anyone's ID, 220+ countries Didit: ID photo and a selfie, on Didit's own page About 30 full checks a month free, then it stops and charges nothing. Sign-up needs a work email
Anyone's ID, when Didit can't The local AI reads the saved photo and code compares the number and name. The photo must show a face or an official emblem, so typed text doesn't pass. It can't spot a forgery, and the badge says so Free
PAN, Indian driving licence, voter ID Cashfree, by number Paid per check, only with its keys
EU VAT number VIES Free, no key
UK company number Companies House Free key
Any company number GLEIF, for companies with an LEI Free, no key
GSTIN, CIN, EIN No free official check: format and check digit, plus GLEIF and the photo Free

The check is a badge, not a gate: nobody is stopped from joining, and owners and HR see how far each ID got. ID photos never go to Claude, whichever mode the AI is in.

With the AI online, what it reads goes to Anthropic: profiles, CVs, chats with Deminic, meeting captions and company details. The terms pages say so while it's on. Captions, embeddings and translations stay on your computer either way. If the key stops working the AI shows as offline, and it never moves to the other engine by itself. Claude also has a monthly limit you set in the console, $20 to start with: past it the AI goes offline until next month. The app counts this itself from each answer, so Anthropic's bill is the real number.

If someone goes offline or closes their last tab, whatever the AI is doing for them stops 15 seconds later, on either engine, and it still counts towards their limits. Moving between pages doesn't stop it, and neither does closing one tab while another is open. Work nobody is waiting for carries on: ID checks, meeting captions and notes, and the daily jobs.

📈 Load test results

Run with Locust on 31 October 2026. These are the numbers on the app's own /load-test page: 10 minutes of simulated people using Deminic at once, with the AI answering at the same time, on one computer.

21,720

requests served

96.03%

answered without failing

800

most people at once

44.33

best requests a second

44

AI answers written

0

crashes

As the crowd grew

People at once Requests a second Half faster than 95% faster than Failed
50 17.82 34.3 ms 142 ms 0% 🟢 Fine
200 40.31 1.97 s 6.03 s 0% 🟡 Struggling
500 42.92 6.63 s 24.1 s 1.4% 🟠 Struggling
800 44.33 12.2 s 30 s 20.5% 🔴 Struggling
Back to 50 33.5 ms 151 ms 0% 🟢 Recovered, with no restart

It tops out at about 44 requests a second. That's one worker process at full stretch: past that, more people don't get more done. Everyone waits longer, and a request that has waited 30 seconds counts as failed.

Is it MVP ready?

MVP ready: the owner's call. The bar, set before the test ran, was four checks:

Check Result
❌ Fine at 200 people at once 95% of requests within 6.03 s (the target was 1 s), 0% failed
✅ No crash None in the whole run
✅ Every data check passed 14 of 14
✅ It recovered by itself 95% of requests within 0.15 s, 0% failed, no restart

It passed three of the four. The owner reviewed the result at 200 people and accepted it on 31 October 2026.

The data and the computer behind these numbers

The flood. Before the test, a database was filled with random data in 45 seconds:

People Companies Shops Products Tasks Colleague reviews Attendance days Payslips
6,000 240 140 4,275 19,979 14,311 83,124 2,369

The computer. One PC ran the app, the database, the AI and Locust together: an Intel Core i7-12700F (12 cores, 20 threads), 48 GB of memory and an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (16 GB). The app ran as one worker process.

The AI. Answers ran on the graphics card through vLLM, up to 8 at once, while the website kept serving everyone else. The median answer took 24.8 s, counted from the question to its last word, including its wait in the queue.

What this doesn't cover. It shows how the app held up under load and whether the data stayed right. It isn't a security audit, and real-money payments weren't part of it. The raw Locust report is in reports/.

🧭 How it fits together

flowchart TB
    B([Your browser]) --> A[Deminic<br/>FastAPI app on port 8000]
    A --> Needed
    A -.-> Optional
    subgraph Needed [Required]
        P[(PostgreSQL + pgvector<br/>accounts and search)]
        R[(Redis<br/>login sessions)]
        C[ClamAV<br/>scans uploads]
    end
    subgraph Optional [Optional]
        V[vLLM<br/>the local AI]
        W[Whisper<br/>live captions]
        T[LibreTranslate<br/>other languages]
    end
    A -.-> Outside
    subgraph Outside [Only if you switch them on]
        L[Claude<br/>the online AI]
        D[Didit, VIES, GLEIF,<br/>Companies House<br/>ID checks]
        F[Cashfree<br/>payments]
    end
Loading

The app runs on your computer and its services run beside it in Docker, all answering on 127.0.0.1 only. If an optional service is down, the app keeps working and turns off what needs it. Nothing reaches the outside services until you switch them on.

Part Built with
Backend Python 3.15, FastAPI, Uvicorn, async SQLAlchemy, asyncpg
Data PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector, Redis 7 (login sessions only)
Frontend Jinja templates, MDB UI Kit, Font Awesome, Leaflet, Chart.js
AI vLLM running Gemma 3 12B on the graphics card, or Claude online
Captions faster-whisper (large-v3-turbo)
Translation LibreTranslate
File safety ClamAV
Load testing Locust
Ports
Service Port
The app 8000
Redis 6379
ClamAV 3310
PostgreSQL 5432
vLLM (AI) 8100
Whisper (captions) 9100
LibreTranslate 5000

🔒 Security

  • Encryption: AES-256-GCM for bank and ID numbers, and chats encrypted at rest
  • Uploads: every file is virus-scanned, and pictures are re-encoded to remove their metadata
  • Logins: one login per account, password rules that refuse common passwords, a limit on wrong sign-up and recovery codes, and an IP ban after 5 wrong admin logins
  • Web: a nonce-only content security policy, CSRF protection and rate limiting, with an overload log
  • Abuse: spam protection for chats and both AI assistants, and an admin console with bans and an IP blocklist
  • Database: the app runs on a login that can only read and write rows
  • Network: Redis has a password, and every service answers on this computer only
  • Staying up: on Windows the server runs on a repaired event loop, so hundreds of open connections or a client hanging up at the wrong moment can't stop it (winloop.py)
  • Keys: kept in .env, tried before they're saved, and never shown again

⚙️ Configuration

Every setting is in .env.example, with a note on what it does. The first run makes your .env from it. These are the ones you're most likely to change:

Setting What it does
APP_NAME The site's name
CONTACT_EMAIL, OWNER_NUMBER How people reach the owner, shown on the site
PORT The port the app listens on (change PUBLIC_URL with it)
MAX_COMPANIES_PER_ACCOUNT How many companies one account can own at a time
OWNER_AWAY_DAYS Days an owner can be away before their companies halt (7)
REQUEST_WINDOW_DAYS Days before an unanswered request to join or leave is declined (30)
CYCLE_DAYS How often salaries are paid, in days
GEOAPIFY_API_KEY, GEOAPIFY_SERVER_KEY Maps, needed to create a company
ADMIN_USERNAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD Turns on the admin console
AI_MODE, ID_VERIFY, PAYMENTS Where the admin console's switches start. Once a switch is used, it decides
VLLM_GPU amd, nvidia or none. Double-click start.cmd again after changing it

Restart the app after changing .env, except for keys pasted in the admin console, which work at once.

Caution

Keep .env safe, and don't change SECRET_KEY. A new key makes saved bank and ID numbers unreadable and hides saved pictures. Your .env is ignored by Git and never leaves your computer.

Project layout 
start.cmd            One click: installs what's missing and starts everything
setup_services.ps1   What start.cmd runs: installs, starts Docker and the services
app.py               Starts the app and its background jobs
winloop.py           The repaired Windows event loop the server runs on
system.py            Config, security, sessions, templates, asset build
tables.py            Database models and migrations
form.py              Form models and validation
apikeys.py           The outside services' keys, read from .env
routers/             Pages and API endpoints
payroll.py, guard.py Salaries, the payroll guard, owners away, requests nobody answered
idcheck.py           The ID checker
deminic.py, grow.py  The AI assistant, AI reviews and the AI engine
aijobs.py            Stops AI work when the person it's for has gone
companyai.py         Promotions and task allotment
shop.py, shopai.py   The marketplace and its AI
meet.py, presence.py Video meetings and live attendance
spam.py, abuse.py    Spam protection and abuse reports
templates/           HTML pages
assets/              CSS and JavaScript sources
static/              Third-party libraries, fonts and images
locales/             Saved translations
reports/             The latest load test, shown at /load-test
vllm_service/        The AI container
whisper_service/     The captions container
docs/                The pictures in this README
myapp/               Python dependencies (uv)
requirements.txt     The same dependencies, for pip
Installing by hand

start.cmd doesn't need this. If you'd rather use pip, you need Python 3.15:

py -3.15 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup_services.ps1
.\.venv\Scripts\python app.py

setup_services.ps1 makes .env, starts the containers and sets up the optional services. It needs Windows, because of Docker Desktop and WSL.

Troubleshooting

Windows asked me to restart. WSL needs one restart when it's first installed. Double-click start.cmd again afterwards and it carries on.

It says an Application Control policy blocked a file. Windows refused to run a file it doesn't trust, and the message names the file. Setup uses python.org's signed Python to avoid this.

The AI's light stays red. It may still be downloading: look for the minimized window. If that window has closed, the reason is in logs/setup_optional.log. After a reboot the AI takes about 4 minutes to start.

It says this computer already has a database. A new .env can't open data made with another one. Put your old .env back and run start.cmd again.

Port 8000 is taken. Set PORT and PUBLIC_URL in .env.

Known gaps
  • One app process only: rate limits, spam limits, live sockets and the AI queue are held in its memory.
  • Cashfree payments and refunds have only been tested against a stand-in server built from Cashfree's documentation, never with real money.
  • Claude, Didit and Companies House have only been tested against stand-in servers built from their documentation, never with real keys.
  • The local AI's ID photo check has only been tested on drawn cards, never on real IDs.
  • If an owner never comes back, their company stays halted until the admin deletes it.
  • The NVIDIA option, the AI's model download on a fresh install, and the WSL and Docker Desktop install steps haven't been tested on a fresh PC.
  • The load test above ran before the latest round of fixes.
  • The test scripts aren't in this repository.

📄 License

Released under the MIT license: anyone can use it, copy it, host it or build on it, as long as the license notice stays with it. It's provided as is, without warranty, and the owner isn't liable for any damages from using it. The terms for using a running site and the owner's contact details are on the app's /terms page.

1442642352.name: mindfulness
1442642352.description: Student-grade companion app for people living with dementia. Not medical care: no warranty, no liability. MIT License.
1442642352.readme_html:
Nobody has to remember a password.
You come in with your face or your fingerprint, and Mindy takes it from there.

Meet Mindy  ·  What it does  ·  See it  ·  Run it  ·  How it fits together  ·  Safety  ·  No liability  ·  License

Caution

This is simply a student-grade project. It is not a medical device and not medical care. It does not replace a doctor, a mental health professional or a caregiver. It can make mistakes, say the wrong thing, or miss something that matters.

It is provided as it is, with no warranty of any kind. The owner of this project, the student who made it, is not liable or responsible for any injury, loss, damage or other harm, from any cause, that comes from using it or from not being able to use it. Anyone who uses it does so at their own risk.

In an emergency, call your local emergency number.


Meet Mindy

Mindy is the heart of the app: a gentle face on the screen who talks, listens and remembers. She tells a person what day it is, reminds them of their plans, tells stories, plays word games and asks how yesterday's walk went. If something seems wrong, she tells the caregiver.

Her lips follow the words of her voice. She blinks, her eyes wander, and her face changes with the mood of what is being said.


When a word slips away

Losing a word in the middle of a sentence is one of the hardest parts of memory loss. Most apps would answer straight away, or wait for words that never come. Mindy does neither.

Every button carries a picture she chooses herself, so it can be recognised without reading. A drop for water, a cup for tea, a bed for a nap.

The real app, recorded on a real graphics card. Only the seconds she spends thinking are cut out.


What it does

For the person


No passwords
Come in with a face or a fingerprint. Nothing to remember.
Today, at a glance
Who you are, the day, the time, and what comes next, in large calm type.
A voice that stays with you
One soft voice across the whole app. Every page can read itself aloud.

Asks, then remembers
"Remind me at five to call Priya" goes on the day, with Undo for 15 minutes.
Your people
Big Call buttons, and "tell my son I'd like to see him" reaches the caregivers.
Help, one touch away
A red button with a slow heartbeat. It works even when everything else is resting.

Games and stories
Stories, gentle word games and a friendly chat, any time.
Show Mindy something
Hold up a photo or an object, and she says what she sees.
Shows the way
Ask how to call your daughter, and she lights up the button to touch.

For the caregiver


What needs you
Every warning for every person, most serious first, with numbered steps.
Told straight away
A scream, a cry for help, a threat or talk of self-harm reaches you in seconds.
Reminders you set
Medicines, meals and walks: daily, on chosen days, or once, with a picture.

Mindy's reflections
Thoughts, feelings and actions from recent talks, with concerns she has noticed.
Messages
What someone asked Mindy to pass on waits on your dashboard until you press Seen.
The care circle
Join someone's circle by ID, by your face, or by your fingerprint.

See it

These are real screens from the app. The household is made up, and the portraits are illustrations drawn from Mindy's own artwork.


A calm home. Who you are, today, and what comes next.
The care dashboard. What needs you, most serious first.

The way in. Two big cards, and Mindy to help.
On a phone. The same calm, in your hand.

Run it

You need Windows 11 with Docker Desktop, uv, a webcam, and for fingerprints Windows Hello or an Android phone. The AI runs on a graphics card, on an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT here.

uv run app.py

That one line starts Docker if needed, then the database, the AI and the voice, then the app at http://localhost:8000. Open it, touch Set up, create the first caregiver, add your face, and you are in.

Settings live in .env, made from .env.example with fresh secrets on the first run. Add your HF_TOKEN there for the model downloads.

Other ways to run it 
uv run app.py --no-services                                     # the services are already running
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\services.ps1 -Status  # what is up
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\services.ps1 -NoAi    # the database only

If it stops at once with "port 8000 is already in use", Mindfulness is already running. Open http://localhost:8000, or close the other copy first.


How it fits together

Her answers stream over a WebSocket one sentence at a time, each already turned into audio, so she starts speaking while the model is still writing. Word timings from the voice become mouth shapes. Every sentence is also read by the server the moment it arrives, so a threat or talk of self-harm reaches the caregivers before the AI has said a word.


Safety and privacy

What stays on this computer: the AI, the voice, the face models and the database all run here. Face pictures, conversations and reminders are not sent to any AI company.

What does not: Chrome and Edge listen through the browser's own speech recognition, which can use its maker's online service. Other browsers, like Brave and Firefox, use whisper on this computer instead. The weather comes from Open-Meteo, and when the browser does not share its location, the town is looked up from this computer's address through ipapi.co. Email and text alerts go through whichever service you set up.

What How it is looked after
The camera A login needs two or more good pictures, no two the same, and every one must match. Look-alikes are sent to their fingerprint or password. The AI checks that a real person is there, not a photo or a screen.
Fingerprints Passkeys (WebAuthn). The device checks the finger and the app only ever receives a signature.
Passwords Optional. Changing one does not ask for the old one, because people with memory loss forget it. Close the session with "I'm done" on a shared tablet.
Limits One budget per person, 60 requests a minute by default (RATE_LIMIT in .env). A patient sees "Let's take a little break", with the Help button still there. Anyone else is told the exact limit. The alarm is never limited.
Caregivers No caregiver can change another caregiver's login. A caregiver who signs up at the welcome screen waits for approval.
The web A strict Content-Security-Policy with no inline scripts, CSRF on every form, server-side sessions, and known host names only. With ENVIRONMENT=production the app refuses to start with test settings.

A printed photo can still pass the camera while the AI is away, so a patient then needs a much closer match, and a caregiver's account stays closed to the camera. Fingerprints are the strong login.

Putting it in front of other people
  • GET /healthz says the app is up. GET /readyz also checks the database. Neither counts against the limit.
  • The app answers only to ALLOWED_HOSTS. Left empty, that means localhost and 127.0.0.1, plus this computer's name and addresses with HOST=0.0.0.0. When set, it replaces those, so list every name the app is opened by.
  • Behind a reverse proxy, name it in TRUSTED_PROXIES, or every visitor looks like the proxy and shares one budget.
  • Other devices need HTTPS. Without it, passwords and the session cookie cross the network unencrypted, and the app warns about that at startup.
  • The limits are counted in memory and start again on a restart. To share the everyday limit between several processes, uv add redis and point RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE at a Redis server.
  • Back up the database and data/photos. The app copies them nowhere.
  • Restart after changing .env, CSS or JS.
Tests

The suites run on a second copy with its own database, so the family's data is never touched. Always pass its address, because some suites default to the live port.

$env:ENVIRONMENT = "test"; $env:PORT = "8010"; $env:POSTGRES_DB = "mindfulness_test"; $env:FACE_LIVENESS = "off"
$env:DATA_DIR = "C:\temp\mindfulness-test"      # its own photos folder
$env:RECOVERY_SHOW_CODES = "true"; $env:SMTP_HOST = "localhost"; $env:SMTP_FROM = "test@example.com"   # for test_password
$env:EXPOSE_QUERY_COUNT = "true"                # for test_queries
$env:RATE_LIMIT = "100000/minute"               # "12/minute" for test_limits, and nothing else then
uv run app.py --no-services

Then, in another window, with a folder holding obama.jpg, obama2.jpg, biden.jpg and two_people.jpg:

Suite What it proves
tests.test_web <faces> <url> The whole story on an empty database. Leaves an enrolled caregiver behind.
tests.test_talk <faces> <url> Live talk, cut-off sentences, reminders and Undo, messages, threats and self-harm, alarms, her ears.
tests.test_password <url> Passwords, email and phone login, recovery codes.
tests.test_carewatch The dashboard's warnings and reminders. Needs POSTGRES_DB=mindfulness_test.
tests.test_queries <faces> <url> No N+1: no page runs more statements with more people. Needs POSTGRES_DB=mindfulness_test.
tests.test_abuse <faces> <url> Junk at every entrance: nothing crashes, and no error hides in the server's log.
tests.test_limits <faces> <url> One budget, the words people see, and what is never limited.
tests.test_face <faces> The face engine, and that a changed model file is refused.
tests.test_liveness <image> The AI's check for photos and screens.
tests.test_passkey <faces> <url> Fingerprints with virtual authenticators. Needs uv run --with playwright and http://localhost:8010.
tests.screenshots <faces> <out> <url> Every page, with console errors. Needs uv run --with playwright.
tests.stress_ai <faces> Hard prompts and bursts: is Mindy polite under pressure?

Run each with uv run python -m. The sign-up limit lives in memory, so restart the copy between suites that sign people up.

Where things are 
app.py                  entry point: services.ps1, then uvicorn
services.ps1            Docker Desktop, database, AI (attach or start)
docker-compose.yml      the database and vLLM
vllm_service/           the AMD/NVIDIA vLLM image recipe
mindfulness/
  config.py             settings from .env
  db.py, models.py      async engine, tables
  security/             headers and CSP, CSRF, sessions, limits, upload ceiling, safe redirects, access log
  auth/                 login, sign-up, enrolment, face engine, matching, liveness, passkeys, passwords
  ai/                   Mindy, her memory, voice, ears, reminders and messages, concerns, button pictures
  care.py               unique IDs and the care circle
  carewatch.py          the care dashboard
  alerts.py             distress alerts to caregivers
  accounts.py           delete account, 30-day retention, purge
  guides.py             the step-by-step guides Mindy shows
  realtime.py           Socket.IO live talk
  web/                  pages, templates, CSS, JS, fonts and icons
tests/                  the suites above
docs/TECHNICAL.md       the full technical notes
docs/readme/            the pictures on this page, and build_art.py, which draws them

Want every detail? The technical notes cover the AI on an AMD card, the live talk, logging, the database and each security decision.

1442642352.readme_excerpt:
**Nobody has to remember a password.**
You come in with your face or your fingerprint, and Mindy takes it from there. [Meet Mindy](#meet-mindy)  ·  [What it does](#what-it-does)  ·  [See it](#see-it)  ·  [Run it](#run-it)  ·  [How it fits together](#how-it-fits-together)  ·  [Safety](#safety-and-privacy)  ·  [No liability](#no-liability)  ·  [License](#license)
> [!CAUTION] > **This is simply a student-grade project.** It is not a medical device and not medical care. It does not replace a doctor, a mental health professional or a caregiver. It can make mistakes, say the wrong thing, or miss something that matters. > > It is provided as it is, with no warranty of any kind. **The owner of this project, the student who made it, is not liable or responsible for any injury, loss, damage or other harm, from any cause, that comes from using it or from not being able to use it.** Anyone who uses it does so at their own risk. > > In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
## Meet Mindy Mindy is the heart of the app: a gentle face on the screen who talks, listens and remembers. She tells a person what day it is, reminds them of their plans, tells stories, plays word games and asks how yesterday's walk went. If something seems wrong, she tells the caregiver. Her lips follow the words of her voice. She blinks, her eyes wander, and her face changes with the mood of what is being said.
## When a word slips away Losing a word in the middle of a sentence is one of the hardest parts of memory loss. Most apps would answer straight away, or wait for words that never come. Mindy does neither. Every button carries a picture she chooses herself, so it can be recognised without reading. A drop for water, a cup for tea, a bed for a nap.
The real app, recorded on a real graphics card. Only the seconds she spends thinking are cut out.

## What it does ### For the person

No passwords
Come in with a face or a fingerprint. Nothing to remember.
Today, at a glance
Who you are, the day, the time, and what comes next, in large calm type.
A voice that stays with you
One soft voice across the whole app. Every page can read itself aloud.

Asks, then remembers
"Remind me at five to call Priya" goes on the day, with Undo for 15 minutes.
Your people
Big Call buttons, and "tell my son I'd like to see him" reaches the caregivers.
Help, one touch away
A red button with a slow heartbeat. It works even when everything else is resting.

Games and stories
Stories, gentle word games and a friendly chat, any time.
Show Mindy something
Hold up a photo or an object, and she says what she sees.
Shows the way
Ask how to call your daughter, and she lights up the button to touch.
### For the caregiver

What needs you
Every warning for every person, most serious first, with numbered steps.

1208565770.readme_html:
🚀 YT Mini: AI Multimodal Video Intelligence System

YT Mini is a high-integrity, multimodal AI application designed for automated video summarization and architectural durability. Built on a production-mirror environment of Arch Linux, it leverages state-of-the-art LLMs and neural captioning to transform video content into structured intelligence.

🧠 AI Multimodal Pipeline

The system utilizes a multi-stage inference engine to "see" and "hear" video content: The process queue is handled by Flask executor and each user is alloted a 60second timeout window Visual Extraction: Custom logic captures 07 key frames per video to provide visual context. Multimodal LLM: Ollama (Micicpm-v) processes Base64 encoded frames for secure image-to-text transmission. Neural Audio: Whisper V3 Turbo provides lightning-fast caption extraction for deep textual understanding. Real-time Updates: SocketIO streams the AI's "thought process" and progress directly to the client UI. 📊 Performance Benchmarks (Locust Verified)

The architecture has been stress-tested to hardware saturation to ensure stability under extreme load. Metric Result Total Requests (10 min window) 354,496 Burst Peak Throughput 688.08 req/s Sustained Equilibrium 504.05 req/s Failure Rate (Under 700 req/s) 0.00% Hardware Bottleneck Analysis

During Phase 2 (Extreme Saturation) at 783.90 req/s, a 19.81% failure rate was recorded. Analysis confirms this was a hardware utility limit: VRAM: Analysis of 7 frames per video exhausted the 12GB VRAM buffer. GIL Limits: Python’s Global Interpreter Lock reached context-switching limits. I/O Wait: Hit the physical caps of the SATA SSD and PostgreSQL socket availability. 🛡️ Security & Infrastructure Data Integrity: SQLAlchemy ORM with parameterized queries to prevent SQL Injection. Defensive Layer: * IP-based Rate Limiting (50 req/min). CSRF Integrity tokens for all state-changing actions. flask-talisman with moderate to strict Content Security Policy. Global context-aware XSS Auto-escaping. Production Stack: * Server: Nginx (Reverse Proxy) + Gunicorn (Eventlet Workers). Database: PostgreSQL 16. Real-time: Flask-SocketIO.

💻 Mirror Production Environment

OS: Arch Linux

CPU: Intel i5-12400F

RAM: 32GB DDR4

GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3060 (12GB VRAM)

Storage: 1TB SATA SSD

🛠️ Usage (Authorized Users Only)

After receiving permission, the stack can be launched via the production protocol:

Start the Infrastructure:
Bash
sudo systemctl start nginx
sudo systemctl start postgresql

Launch the Stack:
Bash
./system/bin/python -m gunicorn -k eventlet -w 1 --bind 127.0.0.1:5000 app:system
